# lance-file binary fixture contents

This supplement currently interprets **v1.lance only**, all 387,133 bytes and 4,097 rows. The two [embedded V2_0 fixtures](rust-lance-file-embedded-fixtures.md) are covered separately; the standard V2_2 fixture remain pending. [Crate](rust-lance-file.md), [V1 codecs](rust-lance-file-v1-codecs.md), [V1 writer](rust-lance-file-v1-writer.md), [V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md), [complete fixture byte map](../L2-files/rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/v1.lance.md), [format contracts](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md), [test workflow](../L4-crosscutting/build-and-test.md).

All binary coordinates use zero-based half-open intervals, written `path@bytes:start-end`; they are byte references, never invented source line numbers. The [inspection report](../analysis/iteration-066-v1-fixture.json), [original bytes](../evidence/binary/v1.lance), [all decoded rows](../evidence/binary/v1-decoded-rows.json) and [offline inspection implementation](../tools/inspect-v1-fixture.mjs) are preserved inside the KB. Inspection asserts every payload and offset against the generator's deterministic rules. The Lance runtime, repository tests and baseline generator have not been executed.

## Provenance and external schema

The checked-in README identifies baseline commit `3a72f8a61e14613f517dded6816d4bfc77817c93`; this is a Git pin, not independent evidence of a released package. The observed SHA-256 is `fa8b3d81b9d4fd4ade5a7c3d077ebf2155664e12b9335e26fac1c0d0774e916c`, matching the pinned README. Regeneration is a distinct baseline workflow and was not performed. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/README.md:3-41; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/v1.lance@bytes:0-387133)

The generator constructs a schema from an Arrow batch, populates dictionary values and writes five slices of at most 1,024 rows. Its NoManifest provider returns `Ok(None)`, so the file contains no self-describing schema. It explicitly requests no statistics fields. Required schema information comes from the fixture generator or another external owner; inferring arbitrary unknown schemas from this binary is unsupported. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:25-36; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:37-100; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:133-157; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:191-206)

| Field ID | Name | External Arrow type / nullable | Stored representation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | id | Int32 / false | Int32 value array |
| 1 | name | Utf8 / true | UTF-8 bytes then absolute Int64 positions |
| 2 | items | List(item:Int32 nullable) / true | Relative Int32 positions, N+1 entries |
| 3 | items.item | Int32 / true | Child Int32 values, no validity |
| 4 | category | Dictionary(Int8,Utf8) / true | Int8 keys; separate dictionary after page table |
| 5 | blob | LargeBinary / true | Inline payload bytes then absolute Int64 positions |

The schema's `name` metadata requests `lance-encoding:compression=none`; category requests `lance-encoding:dict-values-compression=none`; blob marks `lance-encoding:blob=true`. These metadata strings are externally supplied and absent from this binary. In the observed V1 file all blob bytes are inline. The field IDs above are the generator's preorder assignment interpreted against all 30 matching table cells; the file stores neither field names nor data types. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:73-100; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:427-460; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/v1.lance@bytes:386572-387052)

## Exact physical layout

```text
v1.lance: 387133 bytes
+-- [0,386572) five batches, each in field order
|   +-- id values
|   +-- name bytes; absolute Int64 positions
|   +-- list relative Int32 positions; child Int32 values
|   +-- category Int8 keys
|   +-- blob bytes; absolute Int64 positions
+-- [386572,387052) 6 fields x 5 batches x (position,length): 480 bytes
+-- [387052,387064) dictionary UTF-8: greenbluered
+-- [387064,387096) dictionary absolute Int64 positions: 32 bytes
+-- [387096,387100) UInt32 metadata length: 17
+-- [387100,387117) Metadata protobuf: 17 bytes
+-- [387117,387125) Int64 metadata pointer: 387096
+-- [387125,387127) Int16 major: 0
+-- [387127,387129) Int16 minor: 2
+-- [387129,387133) ASCII LANC
```

These intervals exhaust the file without padding, gaps, checksums, embedded manifest or statistics block. Integer buffers in this artifact are little-endian; the current plain/page-table writers copy Arrow native buffers, so the artifact observation is not a proof of portable output on every host endianness. Framing/footer writers explicitly use little-endian operations. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/v1.lance@bytes:0-387133; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:91-117; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:119-144; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:627-651; rust/lance-io/src/traits.rs:83-106)

| Batch | Global row interval | Byte interval | Name nulls | Input list nulls | Input child nulls | Child values | Input category nulls |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | [0,1024) | [0,96588) | 147 | 94 | 186 | 2790 | 79 |
| 1 | [1024,2048) | [96588,193220) | 146 | 93 | 186 | 2793 | 79 |
| 2 | [2048,3072) | [193220,289852) | 146 | 93 | 187 | 2793 | 79 |
| 3 | [3072,4096) | [289852,386452) | 147 | 93 | 186 | 2793 | 79 |
| 4 | [4096,4097) | [386452,386572) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 0 |
| Total | 4097 rows | 386572 data bytes | 586 | 373 | 745 | 11172 | 316 |

Each count follows the generator's modulo rules and is checked against the actual offsets/value buffers; input null intent for lists, child integers and dictionary keys is external information that these V1 buffers lose. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:37-100; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/v1.lance@bytes:0-386572)

## Values, offsets and null semantics

For global row `r` in 0..4097, id is r. Name is null exactly when r%7=0, otherwise the 32-byte ASCII string `value-{r:04}-deterministic-fixture`. The name block concatenates non-null strings; N+1 absolute Int64 positions follow it, and the page pointer addresses those positions rather than the first string byte. The nullable binary reader identifies equal adjacent positions as null, which also means this representation cannot distinguish a nullable empty string from null. All observed non-null names have length32. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:37-42; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:49-89; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:165-178; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:193-233; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/v1.lance@bytes:4096-40360)

Items is originally null when r%11=0, otherwise `[r, r%5==0 ? null : 2*r, 3*r]`. The V1 file writes a list offset increment of0 or3 and child triples `[r, r%5==0 ? 0 : 2*r, 3*r]`. Parent and child validity are not stored. The fixture's expected V1 read therefore maps 373 parent nulls to empty lists and 745 child nulls to zero. This is a frozen compatibility behavior, not a feature to retrofit or silently correct in the legacy writer/reader. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:43-53; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:491-537; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:91-117; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:100-135; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/v1.lance@bytes:40360-55620; AGENTS.md:13-18)

Category is originally null when r%13=0; other rows select red/green/blue by r%3=0/1/2. First appearance orders dictionary values `[green,blue,red]`, hence corresponding keys2/0/1, and null key backing bytes are0. V1 persists those Int8 bytes without validity, so 316 input nulls read as green. The dictionary value block's positions are `[387052,387057,387061,387064]`; a schema that hydrates dictionary bytes needs offset387064 and length3. A reader may instead receive the already populated dictionary values, as the local compatibility test does. The file itself stores no schema field linking category to that block. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:54-68; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/dictionary.rs:36-57; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:93-130; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:115-135; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:467-524; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/v1.lance@bytes:387052-387096)

Blob is the non-null 31-byte `blob-{r:04}-deterministic-payload`. Its N+1 positions are absolute Int64 addresses advancing31 each time. The nullable schema does not introduce nulls in this fixture, and the blob field's metadata does not transform V1 storage into a modern external blob description. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:69-100; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:293-392; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/v1.lance@bytes:56644-96588)

## Table, metadata and footer interpretation

The page table is field-major: cell(field,batch) starts at `386572 + (field*5+batch)*16`. Each cell is two little-endian Int64 values, position then logical length. Id/category/child positions point directly to values; name/blob positions point to absolute-offset arrays; items points to relative positions and reports N+1, not N. The complete 30-cell matrix and every physical data interval are in L2 and the report. Dimensions must come from external schema and metadata; this block has no independent count header. (protos/file.proto:41-61; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:36-144; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/v1.lance@bytes:386572-387052)

The metadata payload is exact hex `120b0080088010801880208120188ccc17`. Byte0 `12` means field2/wire2, byte1 `0b` means packed length11. Packed values are `00`, `8008`, `8010`, `8018`, `8020`, `8120`, decoding `[0,1024,2048,3072,4096,4097]`; byte13 `18` means field3/wire0 and `8ccc17` decodes386572. Field1 is absent, so manifest_position defaults0 (external); field5 statistics is absent. The framing prefix is `11000000`. Footer bytes are `18e8050000000000000002004c414e43`, selecting raw version(0,2), the V1 identity. (protos/file.proto:24-93; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/v1.lance@bytes:387096-387133)

## Evidence and extension limits

The existing `v1_writer_and_reader_are_wire_compatible` test writes five batches with no stats, compares every output byte to the pinned fixture, checks footer identity, reads the pinned bytes with a supplied populated schema and asserts five batches plus the normalized expected values. These are source assertions; they were not run. The KB-side parser establishes static byte meaning and agreement with fixture formulas, not runtime IO, scheduling, cancellation, Arrow implementation behavior or actual historical writer execution. (rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:467-524)

There are no callable symbols, configuration knobs, mutable state or unsafe blocks inside the binary itself. Its consumers are the include_bytes fixture switch and that compatibility test; its producer is the pinned generator. New format functionality belongs to current writers and version contracts. To investigate a changed V1 byte, first locate its L2 interval, decode the complete logical element/offset/cell, then trace the cited frozen encoder or framing path. Do not regenerate from the implementation under test as a substitute for independent baseline evidence. (rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:137-145; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:133-157; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:191-206; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/README.md:34-41; AGENTS.md:13-18)

The [standard V2_0 fixture](rust-lance-file-standard-v20-fixture.md) now has a complete byte/schema/page contract; V2_2 fixture remains pending.

The [standard V2_1 fixture](rust-lance-file-standard-v21-fixture.md) is now fully interpreted, including structural levels, FastLanes bits, all 73 mini-blocks and 575 byte regions; only V2_2 fixture bytes remain pending in lance-file.

# Encoded-file concatenation and validated parts

All 1,587 physical lines are analyzed, including seven test functions and two fixture helpers. This is a complete local module account; Dataset lifecycle/authority, underlying encoder/decoder/IO implementations and binary fixture contents remain incomplete. Tests were read, not run. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1-1587)

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [Shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) · [Version composition](rust-lance-file-composition.md) · [Structural writer](rust-lance-file-structural-writer.md) · [L2 and exact evidence](../L2-files/rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md)

## Responsibility and runtime values

The module copies complete encoded pages into an ordinary output file, relocating buffer offsets and priorities and regenerating metadata/footer. It does not publish a Dataset transaction, choose a fallback, reserve Blob IDs or own source storage. EncodedFileInput holds a scheduler and optional expected physical row count; the expectation is checked later. DataFilePart additionally retains normalized schema, cached metadata and optional Blob lease/target. Neither object pins an ETag/hash or rechecks immutability during copying. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:4-8; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:60-127; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:795-1035; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1172-1180)

BlobTargetId is an arbitrary Arc string compared by value. It is not persisted and does not establish Dataset/base/object-store authority. FileConcatTarget stores an exact version, Arc schema and optional target identity. FileConcatResult separates Written, Reused(index, output metadata) and Unsupported(reason); malformed/missing inputs instead return Err. All public declarations and fields, private helpers and exact generic bounds are cataloged below. ## Entry paths and validation order

1. Ordinary concat_files rejects empty inputs, concurrently reads raw metadata, then returns LegacyVersion if the target or any input is V1. It finalizes all current metadata before shared compatibility. IO/metadata errors can precede the legacy result. Ordinary target Blob fields are unsupported. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:684-712; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1078-1118)
2. DataFilePart::open first checks lease shape, reads full metadata and reconstructs anonymous Blob descriptor children, checks expected rows, rejects Blob v1, validates rectangular metadata and compares normalized/footer counts. Blob v2 descriptor validation happens before requiring a target ID. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:140-225)
3. concat_data_file_parts rejects empty input, compares optional target identities for every part, then sorts declared leases and rejects overlap. It borrows already validated metadata/schema without reopening or checking Blob descriptors again. Touching leases are legal. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1138-1180)
4. Shared preparation rejects read_batch_bytes=0, then checks compatibility and total-row overflow. A single ordinary input is reused with no output factory or writer-option use. Part mode always writes a new file after successful validation, including one part. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:916-955)

| Compatibility sequence | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Expected row count differs | InvalidInput with path/actual/expected |
| Exact version differs | Unsupported VersionMismatch |
| Schema differs from full target or descriptor-projected target | Unsupported SchemaMismatch |
| External metadata validation fails or normalized rows differ from footer | CorruptFile |
| More than one global buffer | Unsupported ExtraGlobalBuffers |
| Column count differs from first input | Unsupported ColumnLayoutMismatch(None) |
| Any column-level buffers | Unsupported ColumnBuffers |
| Physical column index differs | Unsupported ColumnLayoutMismatch(Some(index)) |
| Serialized column-level encoding differs | Unsupported ColumnEncodingMismatch |

Order is per input after baseline encoding serialization. Column encodings compare protobuf Any bytes; page encodings and page counts may differ. These checks precede the output factory, but page ranges and IO response lengths are checked later. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:680-793)

## Blob schema and descriptor boundary

Footer reconstruction finds top-level consecutive runs matching anonymous descriptor children by ID=-1,parent=-1,name,logical type and empty children. It drains those runs and attaches them to childless Blob nodes in preorder. It does not compare child nullability/metadata/encoding, require all missing nodes be repaired or reject unconsumed queue entries. This is a local interpretation of existing footer metadata, not a migration or new persisted format. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:232-302)

Descriptor validation requires distinct nonnegative Blob field IDs, constructs exact physical-column projection, then opens another FileReader with no cache and streams8192 rows/readahead4. Thus Blob part opening can read metadata twice. It validates decoded descriptor arrays; managed Blob payloads are not loaded here. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:316-377)

| Selected nonnull descriptor kind | Required here | Outside this check |
|---|---|---|
| Inline | size must equal0 | position and ID |
| Packed | lease present and ID contained | payload existence, range bounds, size, repeated IDs |
| Dedicated | lease membership and position0 | payload existence and complete-file size |
| External | recognized kind only | URI, base authority, offset and size |

Unknown kinds propagate BlobKind conversion error. Missing named kind/position/size/blob_id fields are CorruptFile; incorrect Arrow types can panic at downcasts. Descriptor child nulls have no separate guard, and blob_uri is not inspected. Lease shape requires1<=start<end, independently of descriptor content. Struct validity intersects row selection; List/LargeList expand only selected valid parents into child offset ranges. Other containers receive no recursive branch here. A malformed Arrow array/selection can panic through indexing/casts; this function relies on typed decoded arrays. Whole leases are checked for overlap even for non-Blob parts that merely carry unused ranges. ## Copying, memory and failure lifecycle

Inputs and physical columns are processed sequentially. Consecutive complete pages are batched by summed payload bytes; the default16MiB threshold is soft because the first page is admitted even when larger. Zero-length buffers consume no read result but still call the writer's empty external-buffer path. Offsets and sums use checked arithmetic; actual range<=EOF is delegated to IO. The scheduler may coalesce/split requests internally, so one submit_request is not a proven single backend read. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:527-543; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:795-892)

Each positive buffer response must match its recorded length exactly. New PageInfo preserves rows and encoding, replaces physical offsets and checked-adds prior input row count to priority. Priority overflow and extra-response errors occur after potential writes. Metadata for all inputs and all output pages is retained even though payload reads are batched. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:893-915; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:937-1011; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1083-1117)

V2_0 structural header columns copy only until output pages exist, then normalize the first header page to total rows,priority0 and truncate to one. Other current versions copy every column and need no final page adjustment. Column-level encoding comes from the first input. An empty external-buffer write aligns the schema descriptor before initialize_with_external_columns and normal finish. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:962-1021; rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:230-276; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/mod.rs:84-132)

The explicit abort runs only for errors inside the copy/finalize/finish async block. Factory and lazy-writer-construction failures occur before that block; cancellation does not reach its error match. Abort returns no Result at this boundary, so no successful deletion/durable rollback is established. A reused or unsupported result never invokes the output factory. Source and output object identity separation is not checked here. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:942-956; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1025-1035; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:261-269)

Core supplies Schema/Field/Blob conventions, errors and cache; Arrow arrays expose descriptor/null/offset structure; lance-encoding provides normalized ColumnInfo/PageInfo and decoder plugins; lance-io provides schedulers, row selectors and writer trait; prost/prost-types provide exact encoding comparison. The std ordered collections make field-ID maps and lease/schema reconstruction deterministic locally, while futures drives concurrent metadata reads and streaming descriptors. No new feature flag or environment variable is defined. Its loader checks stored size before opening parts with expected rows and lease; its target ID builder uses base:id or primary plus filename. These are observed integration snippets, not full Dataset authority/recovery analysis. 1. Ordinary concat_files rejects empty inputs, concurrently reads raw metadata, then returns LegacyVersion if the target or any input is V1. Blob v2 descriptor validation happens before requiring a target ID. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:140-225)
3. concat_data_file_parts rejects empty input, compares optional target identities for every part, then sorts declared leases and rejects overlap. It borrows already validated metadata/schema without reopening or checking Blob descriptors again. Touching leases are legal. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1138-1180)
4. Shared preparation rejects read_batch_bytes=0, then checks compatibility and total-row overflow. A single ordinary input is reused with no output factory or writer-option use. | Compatibility sequence | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Expected row count differs | InvalidInput with path/actual/expected |
| Exact version differs | Unsupported VersionMismatch |
| Schema differs from full target or descriptor-projected target | Unsupported SchemaMismatch |
| External metadata validation fails or normalized rows differ from footer | CorruptFile |
| More than one global buffer | Unsupported ExtraGlobalBuffers |
| Column count differs from first input | Unsupported ColumnLayoutMismatch(None) |
| Any column-level buffers | Unsupported ColumnBuffers |
| Physical column index differs | Unsupported ColumnLayoutMismatch(Some(index)) |
| Serialized column-level encoding differs | Unsupported ColumnEncodingMismatch |

## Blob schema and descriptor boundary

Footer reconstruction finds top-level consecutive runs matching anonymous descriptor children by ID=-1,parent=-1,name,logical type and empty children. It drains those runs and attaches them to childless Blob nodes in preorder. It does not compare child nullability/metadata/encoding, require all missing nodes be repaired or reject unconsumed queue entries. This is a local interpretation of existing footer metadata, not a migration or new persisted format. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:232-302)

Descriptor validation requires distinct nonnegative Blob field IDs, constructs exact physical-column projection, then opens another FileReader with no cache and streams8192 rows/readahead4. | Selected nonnull descriptor kind | Required here | Outside this check |
|---|---|---|
| Inline | size must equal0 | position and ID |
| Packed | lease present and ID contained | payload existence, range bounds, size, repeated IDs |
| Dedicated | lease membership and position0 | payload existence and complete-file size |
| External | recognized kind only | URI, base authority, offset and size |

Unknown kinds propagate BlobKind conversion error. Missing named kind/position/size/blob_id fields are CorruptFile; incorrect Arrow types can panic at downcasts. ## Copying, memory and failure lifecycle

Inputs and physical columns are processed sequentially. Consecutive complete pages are batched by summed payload bytes; the default16MiB threshold is soft because the first page is admitted even when larger. Zero-length buffers consume no read result but still call the writer's empty external-buffer path. Offsets and sums use checked arithmetic; actual range<=EOF is delegated to IO. The scheduler may coalesce/split requests internally, so one submit_request is not a proven single backend read. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:527-543; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:795-892)

Each positive buffer response must match its recorded length exactly. New PageInfo preserves rows and encoding, replaces physical offsets and checked-adds prior input row count to priority. Priority overflow and extra-response errors occur after potential writes. Metadata for all inputs and all output pages is retained even though payload reads are batched. V2_0 structural header columns copy only until output pages exist, then normalize the first header page to total rows,priority0 and truncate to one. Other current versions copy every column and need no final page adjustment. Column-level encoding comes from the first input. An empty external-buffer write aligns the schema descriptor before initialize_with_external_columns and normal finish. The explicit abort runs only for errors inside the copy/finalize/finish async block. Factory and lazy-writer-construction failures occur before that block; cancellation does not reach its error match. Abort returns no Result at this boundary, so no successful deletion/durable rollback is established. A reused or unsupported result never invokes the output factory. Source and output object identity separation is not checked here. (rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:942-956; rust/lance-file/src/concat.rs:1025-1035; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:261-269)

The std ordered collections make field-ID maps and lease/schema reconstruction deterministic locally, while futures drives concurrent metadata reads and streaming descriptors. No new feature flag or environment variable is defined. ## Compressive grammar: required children versus unchecked attributes

Across V2_1/2/3, Flat, InlineBitpacking and Constant compression variants succeed without inspecting widths, optional buffer-compression descriptors, literal bytes or other fields. Variable requires offsets; OutOfLineBitpacking, Fsst, ByteStreamSplit, General, FixedSizeList and PackedStruct require values. Dictionary validates indices first, then items. Each required child is recursively validated; missing compression oneof is InvalidInput. General does not require a compression descriptor here; cardinalities, dimensions, schemes, levels and numeric bounds are not generally checked by these visitors. | MiniBlock | has_large_chunk must be false | must be true | must be true |

| Blob | required recursively validated inner layout | same, exact2.2 grammar | same, exact2.3 grammar |
| Sparse | rejected | rejected | large-chunk and selective nested checks |

# Exact current-version reader grammars

**PARTIAL CRATE COVERAGE.** This supplement fully covers four private exact reader modules (1,368 lines). It defines their local metadata acceptance, error ordering, normalization and projection behavior. Current structural writer lifecycles are covered in the [writer supplement](rust-lance-file-structural-writer.md). The [V2_0/compatibility supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md) covers the array writer and test/generator sources. The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) covers metadata IO, cache use and read dispatch. Delegated IO/decoder scheduling, byte decompression, Dataset integration remains pending; all six binary fixture payloads are interpreted. Source tests were read, not run.

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [Composition](rust-lance-file-composition.md) · [Runtime interfaces](rust-lance-file-runtime.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Tests](../L4-crosscutting/build-and-test.md)

## Accepted identity and validation order

| Reader | Full raw footer accepted | Metadata-index identity | Global buffers | Page representation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V2_0 | (0,3) or (2,0) | V2_0 only | no-op | pb ArrayEncoding, normalized PageEncoding::Legacy |
| V2_1 | (2,1) only | V2_1 only | positions aligned64 | pb21 PageLayout, Structural |
| V2_2 | (2,2) only | V2_2 only | positions aligned64 | pb21 PageLayout, Structural |
| V2_3 | (2,3) only | V2_3 only | positions aligned64 | pb21 PageLayout, Structural |

Identity failures are VersionConflict before global-buffer/column work. Index mismatch diagnostics use the actual index enum's standard footer tuple, while full metadata reports original raw numbers. V2_0 preserves the accepted literal alias in cached major/minor alongside concrete V2_0 identity. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:350-395; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:215-258; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:217-260; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:255-298)

Full V2_1+ finish order is exact footer check, global alignment, column decoding, then cache-object construction. Metadata-index finish checks only identity/global alignment; it does not eagerly decode columns. All cached objects retain both original protobuf column metadata and normalized ColumnInfo plus raw schema, declared num_rows, descriptors, byte accounting and retained global bytes. No finish method reconciles these counts with schema/page rows/file size. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:350-395; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:215-258; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:217-260; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:255-298)

For V2_0, page Any must decode as pb ArrayEncoding, then page offset/size counts must match; column counts and Any are checked afterward. There is no page alignment or recursive ArrayEncoding grammar check in this module. V2_1+ decodes structural syntax, validates exact page grammar, then performs shared page alignment/descriptor construction; after all pages it builds ColumnInfo. ColumnEncoding envelope decoding is not a recursive column-grammar validator. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:30-133; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:161-176; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:163-178; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:201-216; rust/lance-file/src/reader/structural.rs:73-155)

Column batches decode serially, stopping at first error. A checked conversion guards each zero-based index, not the count itself: index u32::MAX is accepted, despite the diagnostic wording more than u32::MAX columns. Empty metadata slices are accepted locally. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:135-148; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:178-191; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:180-193; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:218-231)

## Compressive grammar: required children versus unchecked attributes

Across V2_1/2/3, Flat, InlineBitpacking and Constant compression variants succeed without inspecting widths, optional buffer-compression descriptors, literal bytes or other fields. Variable requires offsets; OutOfLineBitpacking, Fsst, ByteStreamSplit, General, FixedSizeList and PackedStruct require values. Dictionary validates indices first, then items. Each required child is recursively validated; missing compression oneof is InvalidInput. General does not require a compression descriptor here; cardinalities, dimensions, schemes, levels and numeric bounds are not generally checked by these visitors. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:18-100; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:18-106; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:18-89)

V2_1/V2_2 RLE require direct Flat values of8/16/32/64bits with data=None and direct Flat8 run lengths with data=None. They reject wrappers, 128-bit values and any present Flat.data buffer-compression descriptor, including a default descriptor. Flat.data is metadata, not a byte payload (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:419-425). V2_3 instead recursively validates both child trees with the full grammar; it imposes no special Flat8 requirement. V2_1 rejects VariablePackedStruct outright. V2_2/V2_3 validate each packed field.value recursively and accept an empty field list at this gate. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:56-98; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:56-104; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:56-87)

These are local structural acceptance checks, not proof accepted data will decode. Recursive visitors and Blob-layout nesting have no explicit local depth limit; protobuf decoder restrictions are a separate, still unqualified boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:26-159; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:26-161; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:26-199)

## Page-layout matrix

| Layout | V2_1 | V2_2 | V2_3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| MiniBlock | has_large_chunk must be false | must be true | must be true |
| FullZip | required value compression | same | same |
| Constant | inline_value absent; rep/def compression absent | validate optional rep/def; inline value unchecked | same as V2_2 |
| Blob | required recursively validated inner layout | same, exact2.2 grammar | same, exact2.3 grammar |
| Sparse | rejected | rejected | large-chunk and selective nested checks |
| Missing layout | InvalidInput | InvalidInput | InvalidInput |

MiniBlock checks large-chunk flag first, then optional repetition, optional definition, required value and optional dictionary encodings. This is an exact grammar boundary; selecting a newer reader does not mean it accepts the prior miniblock flag. V2_1 can read all-null ConstantLayout even though its composition page list has no constant() mechanism. Read acceptance and writer policy must be documented separately. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:102-159; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:108-161; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:148-199; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/mod.rs:125-134)

V2_3 Sparse requires has_large_chunk and value_compression. Positions are validated only when Explicit; missing sets, missing oneofs and other variants pass here. Validity delegates optional positions. List layers inspect nonempty positions, explicit counts and optional validity; FixedSizeList layers inspect optional validity only. A missing structural layer arm errors, but zero layers pass. Slot totals, ordering, ranges, dimensions and actual buffers are not checked by this visitor. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:91-146)

## Projection differences

V2_0 consumes a header column for every ordinary parent and then its children. Blob/packed fields are opaque. Schema-name selection computes the original whole-schema ID map before pruning, preserving original file indices. Missing mappings are silently omitted; complete schema is still retained. V2_1+ projection wrappers use the shared leaf algorithm with original schema mapping. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:177-232; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:193-213; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:195-215; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:233-253)

For V2_0, a comparable struct's child lengths must match its own header length; the error text about children also covers header/child mismatch. For nonstruct containers, child comparisons become disabled below that node, but the returned length remains the parent header length. The shared leaf algorithm instead derives a container's length from its first child. Both reject too few indices; production helpers reject surplus indices and require equal top-level normalized lengths. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:234-310; rust/lance-file/src/reader/structural.rs:278-357)

V2_0 prepare_projection accepts Full metadata after normal projection validity checks and clones metadata/projection, ignoring IO/cache. Indexed input gets structural validity errors first, then unconditional NotSupported. Its ReadProjection trait method awaits this no-IO preparation and then computes length. Accepting a V2_0 metadata index in finish_metadata_index does not imply indexed loading is usable. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:150-175; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:312-348; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:384-395)

## Local tests and change surface

V2_0 test_projection_length omits production's surplus-index check. V2_1 test helper delegates the shared version, which includes that check. Neither helper is a test case. The V2_1 single grammar test places empty VariablePackedStruct under General then FullZip and checks rejection text. V2_2 rejects a nested RLE using Flat16 run lengths; V2_3 accepts the same shape. These last names mention variable width, but construct fixed-width Flat children, not a Variable node. Tests inspect grammar only, no file bytes or decompression; rejection tests do not assert error variant. No sparse validation fixture appears in the V2_3 file. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/reader.rs:397-415; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:260-304; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:262-308; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:300-341)

Changing nested grammar requires visiting every location that can contain a compressive child, including dictionary indices/items, optional level encodings, packed fields and explicit sparse sets. Keep read acceptance separate from the version writer cascade and maintain all stable contracts. These readers expose no plugin registration seam or environment configuration; ordinary module/trait composition is the extension boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:26-159; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:26-161; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/reader.rs:26-199; AGENTS.md:7-17)

# lance-file runtime boundaries: schema, IO, exact dispatch and writer checks

**PARTIAL CRATE COVERAGE.** This supplement fully covers five local files (1,628 lines): datatypes.rs, io.rs, versions/mod.rs, writer.rs and writer/field_types.rs. Current composition/compression policies and shared structural reader are covered in the [composition supplement](rust-lance-file-composition.md). Exact current reader modules are covered in the [reader supplement](rust-lance-file-readers.md); V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 writers and shared pipeline are covered in the [structural writer supplement](rust-lance-file-structural-writer.md); the separate V2_0 writer and compatibility test/generator sources are covered in the [V2_0 supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md). The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) covers full/indexed metadata IO, caching and read dispatch; delegated scheduler behavior, remaining V2 binary fixture payloads remain pending. Source tests are described, not executed.

[File module](rust-lance-file.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) · [Cookbook](../L4-crosscutting/cookbook.md)

## Schema reconstruction and persistence conversion

Fields(pub Vec<pb::Field>) and FieldsWithMeta{fields:Fields,metadata:HashMap<String,Vec<u8>>} are public. From<&Field> recursively flattens parent then children; From<&Schema> concatenates root subtrees. They preserve supplied IDs/parent IDs and do not validate or assign them. TryFrom<&Fields> for Schema reconstructs iteratively and supplies empty schema metadata; TryFrom<FieldsWithMeta> adds lossily decoded metadata. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:95-129; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:157-314)

```text
protobuf list, parents before children
|-- arena: childless Field + child node indices
|-- ID map: unique ID -> node; duplicate ID -> ambiguous
|   '-- ambiguous parent -> first pre-order DFS match
|-- reverse arena order: take children into parent
'-- roots in input order -> Schema(fields, empty metadata)
    '-- FieldsWithMeta adds the converted schema metadata
```

Unique IDs use expected-linear hash lookups; ambiguous references allocate a DFS stack and may lead to quadratic work. Parent-before-child is enforced, strict flat pre-order is not. Historical duplicates are intentionally retained: a nested duplicate under an earlier root can win over a root encountered earlier in the flat list. Missing parents produce Schema errors with name/IDs; internal arena failures are Internal. No Schema::validate or key/type check follows. Iterative reconstruction does not make recursive flattening or Field destruction stack-safe. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:102-245; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:502-520)

Field metadata bytes are decoded with UTF-8 replacement; nonempty dedicated extension_name overrides its metadata key. Unknown numeric encodings become None; encoding numbers1..4 map Plain/VarBinary/Dictionary/RLE, and encoding writes None as0. The legacy field-kind number is ignored on read and forced0 on write. Primary presence uses positive position or legacy bool->Some(0); clustering uses positive position only and writes its legacy bool=false. Dictionary i64 locations cast unchecked to usize and back; loaded dictionary values are discarded. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:11-94; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:316-344)

Minimal local conversion example, derived from the source doctest (not compiled here):

```rust
use lance_core::datatypes::Schema;
use lance_file::{datatypes::Fields, format::pb};
fn decode_root() -> lance_core::Result<Schema> {
    Schema::try_from(&Fields(vec![pb::Field {
        id: 0,
        parent_id: -1,
        name: "value".to_owned(),
        logical_type: "int32".to_owned(),
        ..Default::default()
    }]))
}
```

The example only establishes reconstruction; it does not validate a complete dataset schema. The source metadata roundtrip unit test uses Schema equality, which ignores top-level metadata, so that test alone cannot prove metadata preservation. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:139-156; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:394-410; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:874-878)

## Encoding IO and retained memory

LanceEncodingsIo is public through the crate reexport. It owns a FileScheduler and starts with an8MiB read chunk target; the consuming setter accepts zero without validation. EncodingsIo promises one Bytes per input range including empties. This adapter preserves empty positions and original order, delegates priority unchanged to FileScheduler and always returns Some for optional bypass/stats handles. Stats replaces the extra recorder on a cloned scheduler; it does not reopen the file. (rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:16-17; rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:12-50; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:56-58; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:40-104; rust/lance-io/src/scheduler.rs:1336-1352)

For a range of length n>limit, generate k=ceil(n/limit) chunks: k-1 chunks of floor(n/k), then a final remainder. This is a target, not a strict cap: n=10,limit=3 yields2,2,2,4. Zero limit divides by zero for nonempty requests; reversed bounds subtract unchecked. No sort/dedup occurs. FileScheduler checks actual split start order, coalesces nearby requests and can split again, so this adapter does not determine physical IOP size. (rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:51-98; rust/lance-io/src/scheduler.rs:1195-1264)

Scheduler submission occurs before returning the adapter's boxed async block, including for an empty split list. Await errors propagate; result-count mismatch is Internal. Unsplit requests return the scheduler Vec directly. Reassembly groups returned Bytes per original request, inserts empty Bytes, cheaply clones single chunks and allocates/copies multiple chunks. It does not verify individual result lengths; retained source chunks overlap the combined allocation. Scheduler queue/cancellation lifetime remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:98-148)

## Exact-version dispatch matrix

Every dispatch takes ConcreteFileVersion; callers resolve Stable/Next separately. There is no ordered comparison or implicit nearest-version fallback. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:4-48)

| Operation family | V1 | V2_0 | V2_1, V2_2, V2_3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Field/name/whole-schema projections, physical counts and data-file column mapping | Own v1 module | Own module | Each own module |
| Current read projection / finish raw metadata | Internal | Own module | Each own module |
| Finish metadata index | VersionConflict(0,2) | Own module | Each own module |
| Decode embedded column metadata | NotSupported | Own module | Each own module |
| Validate global buffers | Successful no-op | Own module | Each own module |
| Copy external column | NotSupported, closure unused | Conditional callback | Always await callback |
| Finalize copied pages | NotSupported | Normalize pages | Successful no-op |
| Open projected reader | NotSupported | Full opener only | Eligible indexed attempt, then full on None |
| Create current/lazy writer; encode embedded/mini batch | NotSupported | Own module | Each own module |

Matrix evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:38-277; rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:285-401. Per-version byte grammars and concrete mechanisms are not inferred from this routing table.

External metadata validation checks whole-schema physical count, projection validity, sequential column.index values, then delegates rectangularity/normalized row count to the exact read projection. Indexed reader opening requires preference plus structural eligibility; an indexed error propagates, while None falls back. V2_0 never invokes the indexed closure. Self-described opening delegates optimistic-tail detection; OpenedFileReader::V1 only retains footer numbers, while Current owns FileReader. ## Writer facade and diagnostics

FileWriter stores one boxed exact V2 writer. FileWriterOptions defaults all three Option fields to None; its local validator rejects only max_page_bytes=Some(0). The Arrow C-interface retention warning is documentation; current structural resolution uses 8 MiB per top-level field or a divided supplied budget, explicit max-page size before environment/default32 MiB, and keep_original_array=false. V2_0 uses the same local option resolution formulas (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:326-356). (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:414-439) PAGE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT=64 and LANCE_FILE_WRITER_MAX_PAGE_BYTES are declared here but used by concrete writers. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:17-77)

write_batches awaits batches sequentially, stops at first error and does not roll back earlier effects. External-column initialization converts every ColumnInfo to protobuf first: both page encoding forms and column encoding become serialized prost Any in DirectEncoding; descriptor pairs unzip in order, page row counts/priorities persist, ColumnInfo.index is omitted. Only then is the concrete initializer called. The facade does not establish schema/column or state consistency. finish returns FileWriteSummary{num_rows,size_bytes}; abort returns unit; tell reports delegated position. Their durability/cleanup guarantees require concrete analysis. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:79-115; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:160-289)

ExpectedTypes is effectively crate-internal despite pub declarations in its private module. It converts expected core fields to Arrow once, remembers the last successful SchemaRef, and compares schemas by value equality. It matches expected columns by name (same-position fast path, name-search fallback); absent fields and extras are outside this checker. It does not inspect array values/nulls. A failed check leaves the prior accepted schema cached. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:17-21; rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:67-114)

The recursive checker compares extension name/metadata when enabled, pairs Struct/List/LargeList/Map/FixedSizeList children by position, ignores names/nullability in those arms and ignores Map sortedness. Blob-v2 Struct/Struct short-circuits child validation after the extension gate; the blob encoder is responsible for descriptor checks. Utf8<-Utf8View and Binary<-BinaryView are directional exceptions. Other types use exact DataType equality, potentially including stricter embedded-field equality. Bare column writes skip only the top-level extension comparison; nested children still compare extensions. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:115-193)

FieldTypeMismatch is publicly reexported and downcastable through Error::InvalidInput source. It retains expected/actual FieldRef and a path constructed from expected names. Dot separators are unescaped. Display prints type plus extension; metadata without an extension name prints as no extension even though comparison can reject it. Contextual concrete writers call type checks before encoder preparation/nullability checks; invalid bare column indices are guarded there rather than in ExpectedTypes::check_column. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:21-65; rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:120-193; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:610-630; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:663-689; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:458-477; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:544-572)

# lance-file runtime boundaries: schema, IO, exact dispatch and writer checks

**PARTIAL CRATE COVERAGE.** This supplement fully covers five local files (1,628 lines): datatypes.rs, io.rs, versions/mod.rs, writer.rs and writer/field_types.rs. Current composition/compression policies and shared structural reader are covered in the [composition supplement](rust-lance-file-composition.md). Exact current reader modules are covered in the [reader supplement](rust-lance-file-readers.md); V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 writers and shared pipeline are covered in the [structural writer supplement](rust-lance-file-structural-writer.md); the separate V2_0 writer and compatibility test/generator sources are covered in the [V2_0 supplement](rust-lance-file-v20-compatibility.md). The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) covers full/indexed metadata IO, caching and read dispatch; delegated scheduler behavior, all six binary fixture payloads are now interpreted; other delegated behavior remains pending. Source tests are described, not executed.

[File module](rust-lance-file.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) · [Cookbook](../L4-crosscutting/cookbook.md)

## Schema reconstruction and persistence conversion

Fields(pub Vec<pb::Field>) and FieldsWithMeta{fields:Fields,metadata:HashMap<String,Vec<u8>>} are public. From<&Field> recursively flattens parent then children; From<&Schema> concatenates root subtrees. They preserve supplied IDs/parent IDs and do not validate or assign them. TryFrom<&Fields> for Schema reconstructs iteratively and supplies empty schema metadata; TryFrom<FieldsWithMeta> adds lossily decoded metadata. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:95-129; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:157-314)

```text
protobuf list, parents before children
|-- arena: childless Field + child node indices
|-- ID map: unique ID -> node; duplicate ID -> ambiguous
|   '-- ambiguous parent -> first pre-order DFS match
|-- reverse arena order: take children into parent
'-- roots in input order -> Schema(fields, empty metadata)
    '-- FieldsWithMeta adds the converted schema metadata
```

Unique IDs use expected-linear hash lookups; ambiguous references allocate a DFS stack and may lead to quadratic work. Parent-before-child is enforced, strict flat pre-order is not. Historical duplicates are intentionally retained: a nested duplicate under an earlier root can win over a root encountered earlier in the flat list. Missing parents produce Schema errors with name/IDs; internal arena failures are Internal. No Schema::validate or key/type check follows. Iterative reconstruction does not make recursive flattening or Field destruction stack-safe. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:102-245; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:502-520)

Field metadata bytes are decoded with UTF-8 replacement; nonempty dedicated extension_name overrides its metadata key. Unknown numeric encodings become None; encoding numbers1..4 map Plain/VarBinary/Dictionary/RLE, and encoding writes None as0. The legacy field-kind number is ignored on read and forced0 on write. Primary presence uses positive position or legacy bool->Some(0); clustering uses positive position only and writes its legacy bool=false. Dictionary i64 locations cast unchecked to usize and back; loaded dictionary values are discarded. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:11-94; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:316-344)

Minimal local conversion example, derived from the source doctest (not compiled here):

```rust
use lance_core::datatypes::Schema;
use lance_file::{datatypes::Fields, format::pb};
fn decode_root() -> lance_core::Result<Schema> {
    Schema::try_from(&Fields(vec![pb::Field {
        id: 0,
        parent_id: -1,
        name: "value".to_owned(),
        logical_type: "int32".to_owned(),
        ..Default::default()
    }]))
}
```

The example only establishes reconstruction; it does not validate a complete dataset schema. The source metadata roundtrip unit test uses Schema equality, which ignores top-level metadata, so that test alone cannot prove metadata preservation. (rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:139-156; rust/lance-file/src/datatypes.rs:394-410; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:874-878)

## Encoding IO and retained memory

LanceEncodingsIo is public through the crate reexport. It owns a FileScheduler and starts with an8MiB read chunk target; the consuming setter accepts zero without validation. EncodingsIo promises one Bytes per input range including empties. This adapter preserves empty positions and original order, delegates priority unchanged to FileScheduler and always returns Some for optional bypass/stats handles. Stats replaces the extra recorder on a cloned scheduler; it does not reopen the file. (rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:16-17; rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:12-50; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:56-58; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:40-104; rust/lance-io/src/scheduler.rs:1336-1352)

For a range of length n>limit, generate k=ceil(n/limit) chunks: k-1 chunks of floor(n/k), then a final remainder. This is a target, not a strict cap: n=10,limit=3 yields2,2,2,4. Zero limit divides by zero for nonempty requests; reversed bounds subtract unchecked. No sort/dedup occurs. FileScheduler checks actual split start order, coalesces nearby requests and can split again, so this adapter does not determine physical IOP size. (rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:51-98; rust/lance-io/src/scheduler.rs:1195-1264)

Scheduler submission occurs before returning the adapter's boxed async block, including for an empty split list. Await errors propagate; result-count mismatch is Internal. Unsplit requests return the scheduler Vec directly. Reassembly groups returned Bytes per original request, inserts empty Bytes, cheaply clones single chunks and allocates/copies multiple chunks. It does not verify individual result lengths; retained source chunks overlap the combined allocation. Scheduler queue/cancellation lifetime remains pending. (rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:98-148)

## Exact-version dispatch matrix

Every dispatch takes ConcreteFileVersion; callers resolve Stable/Next separately. There is no ordered comparison or implicit nearest-version fallback. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:4-48)

| Operation family | V1 | V2_0 | V2_1, V2_2, V2_3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Field/name/whole-schema projections, physical counts and data-file column mapping | Own v1 module | Own module | Each own module |
| Current read projection / finish raw metadata | Internal | Own module | Each own module |
| Finish metadata index | VersionConflict(0,2) | Own module | Each own module |
| Decode embedded column metadata | NotSupported | Own module | Each own module |
| Validate global buffers | Successful no-op | Own module | Each own module |
| Copy external column | NotSupported, closure unused | Conditional callback | Always await callback |
| Finalize copied pages | NotSupported | Normalize pages | Successful no-op |
| Open projected reader | NotSupported | Full opener only | Eligible indexed attempt, then full on None |
| Create current/lazy writer; encode embedded/mini batch | NotSupported | Own module | Each own module |

Matrix evidence: rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:38-277; rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:285-401. Per-version byte grammars and concrete mechanisms are not inferred from this routing table.

External metadata validation checks whole-schema physical count, projection validity, sequential column.index values, then delegates rectangularity/normalized row count to the exact read projection. Indexed reader opening requires preference plus structural eligibility; an indexed error propagates, while None falls back. V2_0 never invokes the indexed closure. Self-described opening delegates optimistic-tail detection; OpenedFileReader::V1 only retains footer numbers, while Current owns FileReader. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:50-107; rust/lance-file/src/versions/mod.rs:279-326; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1117-1144; rust/lance-file/src/reader.rs:1542-1555)

## Writer facade and diagnostics

FileWriter stores one boxed exact V2 writer. FileWriterOptions defaults all three Option fields to None; its local validator rejects only max_page_bytes=Some(0). The Arrow C-interface retention warning is documentation; current structural resolution uses 8 MiB per top-level field or a divided supplied budget, explicit max-page size before environment/default32 MiB, and keep_original_array=false. V2_0 uses the same local option resolution formulas (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:326-356). (rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:414-439) PAGE_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT=64 and LANCE_FILE_WRITER_MAX_PAGE_BYTES are declared here but used by concrete writers. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:17-77)

write_batches awaits batches sequentially, stops at first error and does not roll back earlier effects. External-column initialization converts every ColumnInfo to protobuf first: both page encoding forms and column encoding become serialized prost Any in DirectEncoding; descriptor pairs unzip in order, page row counts/priorities persist, ColumnInfo.index is omitted. Only then is the concrete initializer called. The facade does not establish schema/column or state consistency. finish returns FileWriteSummary{num_rows,size_bytes}; abort returns unit; tell reports delegated position. Their durability/cleanup guarantees require concrete analysis. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:79-115; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:160-289)

ExpectedTypes is effectively crate-internal despite pub declarations in its private module. It converts expected core fields to Arrow once, remembers the last successful SchemaRef, and compares schemas by value equality. It matches expected columns by name (same-position fast path, name-search fallback); absent fields and extras are outside this checker. It does not inspect array values/nulls. A failed check leaves the prior accepted schema cached. (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:17-21; rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:67-114)

The recursive checker compares extension name/metadata when enabled, pairs Struct/List/LargeList/Map/FixedSizeList children by position, ignores names/nullability in those arms and ignores Map sortedness. Blob-v2 Struct/Struct short-circuits child validation after the extension gate; the blob encoder is responsible for descriptor checks. Utf8<-Utf8View and Binary<-BinaryView are directional exceptions. Other types use exact DataType equality, potentially including stricter embedded-field equality. Bare column writes skip only the top-level extension comparison; nested children still compare extensions. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:115-193)

FieldTypeMismatch is publicly reexported and downcastable through Error::InvalidInput source. It retains expected/actual FieldRef and a path constructed from expected names. Dot separators are unescaped. Display prints type plus extension; metadata without an extension name prints as no extension even though comparison can reject it. Contextual concrete writers call type checks before encoder preparation/nullability checks; invalid bare column indices are guarded there rather than in ExpectedTypes::check_column. (rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:21-65; rust/lance-file/src/writer/field_types.rs:120-193; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:610-630; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:663-689; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:458-477; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:544-572)

The deterministic4097-row input and five batch writes are specified in the L2 contract. Each ColumnMetadata begins tag1 Encoding containing tag2 DirectEncoding/tag1 bytes; those bytes encode Any(type_url=/lance.encodings.ColumnEncoding,value=...). Values is0a00 for columns0..4; Blob(inner Values) is1a040a020a00 for column5. The wrappers consume43/47 bytes. Repeated Page tag2 contains packed absolute offsets tag1, packed unpadded sizes tag2, logical length tag3 and Encoding tag4 with Any type_url=/lance.encodings.ArrayEncoding. Priority5 and column buffers are absent. Array oneof tags are Flat1,Nullable2,List4,Binary6,Dictionary7,PackedStruct9. Flat carries bits1,Buffer2 and optional Compression3; Buffer index1 and type2 default0. Nullable NoNull1 carries values1; SomeNull2 carries validity1/values2. List carries offsets1,A2,num_items3; Binary indices1,bytes2,A3; Dictionary indices1,items2,count3; PackedStruct repeats children1 and carries packed Buffer2. (protos/file2.proto:138-216; protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:44-155; protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:174-188; protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:246-271; protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:308-358; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/v2_0.lance@bytes:619655-706005)

Use the full map to classify byte mismatches as payload/null encoding, batching/page partition, alignment, schema, metadata or footer. Preserve the stable V2_0 contract using existing pinned historical bytes; changing current writer output is not a reason to regenerate the oracle. The existing compatibility harness checks exact byte equality for stable versions, footer identity and decoded batch equality. Encoding implementations are contextual reads only; do not treat this supplement as a complete change recipe for unreviewed codecs. [Offline parser](../tools/analyze-standard-v20-fixture.mjs) and [independent assembler](../tools/verify-standard-v20-reconstruction.mjs) validate artifact content, not Lance runtime behavior. (rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:232-295; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:352-399; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/README.md:10-41)

The [standard V2_1 fixture](rust-lance-file-standard-v21-fixture.md) is now fully interpreted, including structural levels, FastLanes bits, all 73 mini-blocks and 575 byte regions; only V2_2 fixture bytes remain pending in lance-file.

Complete local scope: five files / 854 physical lines, including five tests. Concrete binary/plain/dictionary codecs are covered in the [codec supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-codecs.md); the [full V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md) is covered; the [V1 binary fixture](rust-lance-file-binary-fixtures.md) is fully interpreted; standard V2_2 fixture remain pending. ## Responsibilities and physical identity

The facade publicly owns encoding,format,page_table,reader,writer modules and V1 physical projection helpers. Its documentation declares accepted footer(0,0..=2) and write identity(0,2); the already analyzed exact-version parser maps those identities. The format child forwards metadata only. These files do not select current encoder strategies, commit manifests, publish a Dataset version or implement backend durability. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:1-24) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/mod.rs:1-4) (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:172-272)

~~~text
v1
|-- mod: preorder Field IDs and physical-column projection
|-- encoding: value-codec dispatch and dictionary write/hydration
|   |-- plain / binary / dictionary: concrete codecs covered separately
|-- format/metadata: cumulative batch offsets and protobuf conversion
|-- page_table: sparse map <-> dense field-major pair matrix
+-- reader / writer: full local lifecycle covered in supplements
`-- writer/statistics: full algorithms and test oracles covered in supplement
~~~

The tree follows the public module declarations and dependencies. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:10-23) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:16-33)

## Projection and field mapping

Visit fields in preorder, emitting the parent and then children. Blob and packed-struct fields each occupy one slot and stop recursion, while ordinary struct/container parents also occupy slots even when they have no data page. data_file_columns returns original signed IDs paired with consecutive signed physical indices from0. Counter/count arithmetic is unchecked. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:72-116)

The private BTreeMap casts IDs/indices to u32; repeated IDs retain the final column value. projection_from_field_ids clones the entire supplied schema into an Arc and appends only mapped fields, silently omitting missing mappings. It does not validate empty/repeated/out-of-bounds indices or remove unmatched schema fields. Column-name projection builds the full original mapping before delegating Schema::project, then selects original physical indices. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:25-71) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:93-116)

## Dictionary dispatch and mutation order

read_binary_array accepts exactly Utf8,Binary,LargeUtf8,LargeBinary, converts parameters first and dispatches to the corresponding BinaryDecoder; other types return InvalidInput. read_fixed_stride_array checks the local fixed-stride predicate, returns Schema on false, constructs PlainDecoder, then converts parameters and awaits get. Neither wrapper independently checks offsets or response sizes. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:35-90)

write_schema_dictionaries scans every ID from0 through max_field_id, skipping holes/nondictionaries. Missing dictionary metadata is IO; missing values is InvalidInput. The actual array type chooses numeric PlainEncoder or binary-like BinaryEncoder; unsupported values give Schema. Only successful encode updates offset/length. Earlier writes and mutations survive later errors; no transaction, shutdown or abort is provided. Cost includes sparse ID-span traversal and repeated schema lookup. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:92-132)

Hydration recursively processes nondictionary roots/children in order. For a dictionary it uses the schema value type, reads the entire stored region and replaces values, even when values was already Some. Binary values use nullable=true; only eight signed/unsigned integer types take the fixed-stride branch. It does not recurse below a dictionary node. async_recursion boxes recursion without explicit task spawning; successful earlier fields remain mutated on error/cancellation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:134-192)

Write and read predicates are asymmetric. The write side asks is_numeric rather than the read side's explicit integer whitelist. The local is_binary_like also accepts Utf8View/BinaryView, which the four-type binary reader rejects. Concrete BinaryEncoder also rejects both view types; PlainEncoder writes fixed-width numeric buffers, while hydration retains its narrower integer whitelist. Complete codec contracts and test limits are now documented separately. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-115) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:47-70) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:116-127) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:143-176) (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:99-142)

Metadata stores Vec<i32> cumulative batch offsets, usize page-table position, Option manifest position and optional statistics. Empty offsets report0batches/rows; otherwise batches=len-1 and rows=last cast to usize. push_batch_length seeds0 and appends an unchecked signed sum. Negative/zero lengths and malformed sentinel vectors are not rejected. get_offset can access the terminal sentinel; get_batch_length computes next-current with current default0, including the unusual negative-ID boundary. Protobuf conversion clones offsets and statistics IDs, casts positions unchecked and flattens only statistics fields, dropping schema-level metadata. Missing manifest position encodes0, while decode always yields Some, including Some(0). Wire0 means externally stored manifest; the object converter does not normalize it back to None. Out-of-file rows can form terminal batch num_batches; nonempty indices with no offsets panic. range_to_batches unwraps the last offset and checks only end<=length, then binary-searches start cast to i32 and forms clamped subranges. These are helper contracts. The observed V1 reader returns an empty RecordBatch for Range::is_empty before calling range_to_batches, and take checks grouped batch_id against num_batches afterward. PageInfo holds position and logical length as usize; observed fixed/binary/dictionary writers use the number of array elements, not encoded byte count. PageTable privately owns BTreeMap<i32,BTreeMap<i32,PageInfo>>. set accepts arbitrary signed keys and overwrites; get distinguishes absent None from explicit Some(0,0).
