## Responsibilities and physical identity

The facade publicly owns encoding,format,page_table,reader,writer modules and V1 physical projection helpers. Its documentation declares accepted footer(0,0..=2) and write identity(0,2); the already analyzed exact-version parser maps those identities. The format child forwards metadata only. These files do not select current encoder strategies, commit manifests, publish a Dataset version or implement backend durability. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:1-24) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/mod.rs:1-4) (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:172-272)

~~~text
v1
|-- mod: preorder Field IDs and physical-column projection
|-- encoding: value-codec dispatch and dictionary write/hydration
|   |-- plain / binary / dictionary: concrete codecs covered separately
|-- format/metadata: cumulative batch offsets and protobuf conversion
|-- page_table: sparse map <-> dense field-major pair matrix
+-- reader / writer: full local lifecycle covered in supplements
`-- writer/statistics: full algorithms and test oracles covered in supplement
~~~

The tree follows the public module declarations and dependencies. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:10-23) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:16-33)

## Projection and field mapping

Visit fields in preorder, emitting the parent and then children. Blob and packed-struct fields each occupy one slot and stop recursion, while ordinary struct/container parents also occupy slots even when they have no data page. data_file_columns returns original signed IDs paired with consecutive signed physical indices from0. Counter/count arithmetic is unchecked. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:72-116)

The private BTreeMap casts IDs/indices to u32; repeated IDs retain the final column value. projection_from_field_ids clones the entire supplied schema into an Arc and appends only mapped fields, silently omitting missing mappings. It does not validate empty/repeated/out-of-bounds indices or remove unmatched schema fields. Column-name projection builds the full original mapping before delegating Schema::project, then selects original physical indices. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:25-71) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:93-116)

## Dictionary dispatch and mutation order

read_binary_array accepts exactly Utf8,Binary,LargeUtf8,LargeBinary, converts parameters first and dispatches to the corresponding BinaryDecoder; other types return InvalidInput. read_fixed_stride_array checks the local fixed-stride predicate, returns Schema on false, constructs PlainDecoder, then converts parameters and awaits get. Neither wrapper independently checks offsets or response sizes. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:35-90)

write_schema_dictionaries scans every ID from0 through max_field_id, skipping holes/nondictionaries. Missing dictionary metadata is IO; missing values is InvalidInput. The actual array type chooses numeric PlainEncoder or binary-like BinaryEncoder; unsupported values give Schema. Only successful encode updates offset/length. Earlier writes and mutations survive later errors; no transaction, shutdown or abort is provided. Cost includes sparse ID-span traversal and repeated schema lookup. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:92-132)

Hydration recursively processes nondictionary roots/children in order. For a dictionary it uses the schema value type, reads the entire stored region and replaces values, even when values was already Some. Binary values use nullable=true; only eight signed/unsigned integer types take the fixed-stride branch. It does not recurse below a dictionary node. async_recursion boxes recursion without explicit task spawning; successful earlier fields remain mutated on error/cancellation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:134-192)

Write and read predicates are asymmetric. The write side asks is_numeric rather than the read side's explicit integer whitelist. The local is_binary_like also accepts Utf8View/BinaryView, which the four-type binary reader rejects. Concrete BinaryEncoder also rejects both view types; PlainEncoder writes fixed-width numeric buffers, while hydration retains its narrower integer whitelist. Complete codec contracts and test limits are now documented separately. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/binary.rs:91-105; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding/plain.rs:90-115) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:47-70) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:116-127) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:143-176) (rust/lance-arrow/src/lib.rs:99-142)

The table manifest writer and schema-hydration adapter call these helpers only for ConcreteFileVersion::V1. The complete [V1 writer](rust-lance-file-v1-writer.md) now establishes provider/finish/error ordering: data page table, statistics, dictionaries/provider schema, Metadata and magics, followed by shutdown. (rust/lance-table/src/io/manifest.rs:212-230; rust/lance-table/src/format/manifest.rs:619-631; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:627-651)

## Metadata and logical row grouping

Metadata stores Vec<i32> cumulative batch offsets, usize page-table position, Option manifest position and optional statistics. Empty offsets report0batches/rows; otherwise batches=len-1 and rows=last cast to usize. push_batch_length seeds0 and appends an unchecked signed sum. Negative/zero lengths and malformed sentinel vectors are not rejected. get_offset can access the terminal sentinel; get_batch_length computes next-current with current default0, including the unusual negative-ID boundary. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:14-33) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:85-123)

Protobuf conversion clones offsets and statistics IDs, casts positions unchecked and flattens only statistics fields, dropping schema-level metadata. Missing manifest position encodes0, while decode always yields Some, including Some(0). Wire0 means externally stored manifest; the object converter does not normalize it back to None. Statistics schema decoding can fail; remaining shape/monotonicity/range validation is absent. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:34-78) (protos/file.proto:25-93)

group_indices_to_batches clones and sorts input despite its sorted-input precondition comment. It preserves duplicate indices but loses original order, scans batch ends, groups in ascending batch ID and subtracts start offsets. Out-of-file rows can form terminal batch num_batches; nonempty indices with no offsets panic. range_to_batches unwraps the last offset and checks only end<=length, then binary-searches start cast to i32 and forms clamped subranges. Empty/reversed/overflow/malformed-offset cases are not fully guarded. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:124-194)

These are helper contracts. The observed V1 reader returns an empty RecordBatch for Range::is_empty before calling range_to_batches, and take checks grouped batch_id against num_batches afterward. Do not turn a missing helper check into an assertion that every public reader call exposes it. The complete reader is now covered in the [reader supplement](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md), including sorted grouping, selector differences, cache assumptions and constructor validation limits. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/reader.rs:342-396)

## Page-table representation and resource behavior

PageInfo holds position and logical length as usize; observed fixed/binary/dictionary writers use the number of array elements, not encoded byte count. PageTable privately owns BTreeMap<i32,BTreeMap<i32,PageInfo>>. set accepts arbitrary signed keys and overwrites; get distinguishes absent None from explicit Some(0,0). (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:16-35) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:147-160) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/writer/mod.rs:393-459)

On disk, table dimensions are implicit: inclusive min..=max field IDs and num_batches from surrounding schema/metadata. Each field has consecutive batches, each containing position and length as signed64 values; missing/struct slots emit0,0. For valid dimensions, values count=2*(max-min+1)*num_batches and byte count=16*(max-min+1)*num_batches. No header or dimension vector is written here. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:36-92) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:94-145) (protos/file.proto:41-59)

load rejects max<min as Internal, then decodes the entire Int64 array and expands every cell into maps, including holes. Negative dimensions/values, arithmetic overflow and actual decoded shape are not independently validated; casts/downcasts/indexing rely on external invariants. Zero batches create nonempty outer maps with empty inner maps. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:53-92)

write rejects empty outer maps and supplied min above observed minimum as InvalidInput. After tell it derives batch count=max batch key+1, builds two values per cell, writes the Arrow values buffer directly and returns starting position. The builder initially reserves only one element per cell. A loaded zero-batch table panics at the max-batch unwrap; sparse large IDs can amplify memory and bytes. This method has no explicit endian conversion, alignment, framing, flush, shutdown, abort or cancellation cleanup. It does not establish atomic persistence. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:103-145)

## Tests, dependencies and extension boundary

Two metadata tests assert one index-group example and four valid range splits. Three page-table tests assert set/get, missing-cell zeros after write/read and three error variants/messages. The roundtrip test starts expected from actual.clone and overwrites fourteen holes; six populated values lack independent expectations. No local tests cover dictionary dispatch, projection edge cases, metadata object presence roundtrip, malformed offsets, negative dimensions, zero-batch rewrite or partial IO. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/format/metadata.rs:209-255) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/page_table.rs:162-287) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/encoding.rs:186-192) (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v1/mod.rs:102-116)

Dependencies are core Schema/Field/error/DeepSizeOf, file protobuf/schema adapters, Arrow arrays/builders/type predicates, IO Reader/Writer/ProtoStruct/ReadBatchParams, Tokio write extension and async-recursion. No local feature flag, environment variable or global mutable cache is declared. Reader/Writer/ProtoStruct are existing boundaries; these five files introduce no new extensible trait. Preserve historical behavior under the repository's frozen legacy policy, and use released historical fixtures for any explicitly required legacy repair. # V2_0 writer and exact-version compatibility harness

**PARTIAL CRATE COVERAGE.** This supplement covers 1,997 lines across the concrete V2_0 writer, testing helpers, compatibility tests and three fixture-provenance/generator files. The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) covers current reader IO/cache orchestration. Binary fixture payloads, delegated scheduling, legacy writer/reader internals and encoding byte algorithms remain pending. Tests and generators were read, not run.

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [Structural writers](rust-lance-file-structural-writer.md) · [Reader grammar](rust-lance-file-readers.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) · [Build and tests](../L4-crosscutting/build-and-test.md)

## Concrete V2_0 ownership and initialization

Writer owns its own object writer, optional schema/type cache, field encoders, physical column metadata/mapping, per-field and aggregate row counts, global descriptors, schema metadata, boxed ArrayFieldEncodingStrategy, options and spill state. It does not compose the shared structural pipeline. Public Writer is reexported from its exact-version parent; the footer helper is effectively internal and reached through parent embedded-batch functions. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:153-218; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/mod.rs:21-32; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:852-856)

```text
V2_0 Writer
|-- ArrayFieldEncodingStrategy -> BatchEncoder -> FieldEncoder list
|-- schema + expected types + schema metadata
|-- physical column metadata + field mapping
|-- per-field counts -> aggregate maximum/logical length
|-- ObjectWriter + user global-buffer descriptors
'-- optional spill: Pending(store,path) -> Active(sidecar,chunk index)
```

Eager construction creates lazy state then initializes. Lazy construction stores inputs and allocates the default strategy without validation or IO. Initialization validates explicit options, computes cache/page limits, validates schema and constructs BatchEncoder before installing encoders/metadata/mapping. It divides a supplied total cache budget by top-level field count; with an empty schema this can divide by zero before schema validation. Defaults are 8 MiB per root field, 32 MiB max page, keep_original_array=false and alignment64. An explicit max-page value wins over the environment; malformed environment text warns and defaults, missing/non-Unicode text silently defaults, and an environment value of zero bypasses the explicit Some(0) rejection. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:184-218; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:326-369; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:56-65)

## Preparation and row mutation

write_batch initializes from its first Arrow schema, checks ExpectedTypes, selects every required field by name and prepares every field array before testing for an empty batch or the single-batch u32 limit. Missing fields fail even for empty batches. FieldEncoder::prepare_array defaults to identity and documents preparation before state mutation; concrete validation/transformation remains encoder-defined. No separate recursive nullability walk appears in this writer. The structural pipeline instead performs its own logical-nullability validation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:313-324; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:371-400; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:451-476; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:175-183; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:598-627)

Encoding snapshots each field's old row number, calls maybe_encode, writes out-of-line buffers, then checks aggregate u64 overflow. Counters advance before ordered page tasks and flush finish, so later failure does not rewind them. Batch counters use original batch.num_rows while encoding uses prepared array lengths; the caller/encoder relationship must preserve these lengths. write_column checks schema/index/input size/type, prepares one array, returns if that prepared array is empty, then advances only that field by its prepared length with unchecked addition and updates the aggregate maximum. A previously initialized lazy writer satisfies its schema check despite the explicit-schema wording in the error. Unequal root-field lengths are allowed. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:402-506; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:507-584)

FuturesOrdered emits task results in insertion order; pages are written sequentially, followed by writer flush. The first error stops the loop and drops remaining local futures. The code comment describes flush as observing failed uploads without waiting for all in-flight uploads; backend implementation, spawned-work cancellation and durability are still outside this scope. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:279-300)

## Buffer placement, spill and completion

Ordinary page, batch-external, global and column buffers get trailing 0x48 padding based on their payload length to64. Their starts are not repaired. V2_0 write_external_buffer writes completely raw at current position, unlike the structural sink's leading-zero alignment. Page metadata records raw lengths and wraps either page-description family in Any/Direct without checking the exact V2_0 grammar. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:41-41; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:231-262; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:703-708; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:831-849; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:352-360)

Spill threshold per column is max(256 KiB/max(column_count,1),64). One message can overshoot; buffers retain capacity and chunk descriptors grow. Pending is removed before awaited sidecar creation, after page payload IO. A failed creation loses pending state. Finish removes metadata/spill state, shuts down and reopens the sidecar, reconstructs all pages for each column and replaces that column's prior page vector. Late spill can therefore discard descriptions retained before activation. Cleanup is explicitly caller-owned and no local deletion occurs. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:48-146; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:219-228; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:263-275; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:597-630)

finish flushes encoders, consumes/finishes them if present, writes descriptor and user-global table entries, column metadata, column offset table, global offset table, footer, then awaits shutdown. Descriptor and column metadata are raw protobuf bytes; each offset-table entry is a 16-byte LE(position,length) pair. Schema metadata is drained and blobs unloaded before descriptor IO. External-metadata initialization bypasses validation and replaces schema/metadata/aggregate rows without rebuilding encoder, type-cache, mapping or field-count state. It can support footer-only external output, but subsequent ordinary writes require coherent state the initializer does not establish. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:586-709; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:768-829)

Two position assumptions need preservation: finish_writers writes out-of-line buffers raw while the planner advances virtual positions by payload plus padding; column-buffer offsets advance by payload length while actual writes include padding. Multiple unaligned buffers can violate those assumptions. These are source deductions, not evidence that current encoder producers emit such shapes. The final physical-column count mismatch panics unconditionally. No finished flag or rollback protects repeat calls; abort is an empty async body and does not drop the writer. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:711-759; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:831-834; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:130-159)

## Exact footer identity

| Footer-relative bytes | Standard V2_0 | Embedded V2_0 |
|---|---|---|
| 0–7 | column metadata start, LEu64 | same meaning |
| 8–15 | column offset table start, LEu64 | same meaning |
| 16–23 | global offset table start, LEu64 | same meaning |
| 24–27 | global-buffer count, LEu32 | zero in mini; one in self-described |
| 28–31 | physical-column count, LEu32 | page_table length |
| 32–33 | major0, LEu16 | major2, LEu16 |
| 34–35 | minor3, LEu16 | minor0, LEu16 |
| 36–39 | LANC | LANC |

These literal branches are independent implementations. The version decoder accepts both as V2_0, and tests distinguish standard and embedded mappings. concat_lance_footer copies input bytes and given page/column descriptors, optionally appends a cloned core schema without blob unloading, then metadata/tables/footer. It ignores ColumnInfo.index and top_level_columns and does not validate supplied buffer positions or grammar. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:812-828; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:852-952; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:226-262; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:379-448)

## Compatibility fixture and test oracles

The deterministic input has 4,097 rows and five fields: Int32 IDs, nullable UTF8 names (every7th null), nullable Int32 lists (every11th null, every5th second child null), nullable Int8/UTF8 dictionary keys (every13th null), and nonnull LargeBinary payloads in a nullable blob-marked field. Compression metadata disables name and dictionary-value compression. Standard writers receive five batches of up to1,024 rows; embedded V2_0 uses only id/name for the first257 rows. (rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:36-98; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:232-315; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:401-408)

Stable cases compare complete current bytes to baseline includes, assert exact footer identity and read the baseline through the current reader. Read assertions include at least one multi-page physical column, full row count/schema equality and ordered value/null equality. Blob comparison ignores physical bytes under nulls. V2_3 instead writes twice in the same revision and checks equal bytes plus roundtrip; it has no checked historical fixture. The V1 test explicitly expects null lists as empty, null child integers as zero and null dictionary keys as green. The full V1 reader and writer are now independently traced in their supplements; this test still establishes only the stated fixture oracle. (rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:100-230; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:318-524)

FsFixture exposes a local store, temp path and testing scheduler. write_lance_file collects the entire input, adds foo=bar to writer schema, finishes and returns original schema/data/mapping. read_lance_file requires that metadata, reads RangeFull with batch1024/readahead16 and collects all output. count_lance_file fully decodes/collects then sums rows. All use unwrap/assert rather than a fallible public result. The original returned schema does not receive the writer's added metadata. test_cache creates a fresh128MiB cache. (rust/lance-file/src/testing.rs:22-123)

## Provenance and generator failure boundaries

README pins baseline commit `3a72f8a61e14613f517dded6816d4bfc77817c93`, lists six SHA-256 values and requires using baseline writers for independent evidence. Local Git metadata confirms that commit exists; the six hashes match the inventory snapshot. No regeneration has been performed. The [V1 fixture](rust-lance-file-binary-fixtures.md) is now fully interpreted; both [embedded V2_0 fixtures](rust-lance-file-embedded-fixtures.md) are also fully interpreted, and the standard V2_2 binary payloads remain pending. The pin identifies a commit and is not, by itself, proof of a released-package fixture. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/README.md:3-41)

The Python script checks exact HEAD and initial clean status, copies the Rust example into the baseline, then runs two separate Cargo processes with separate outputs and one shared isolated target directory. It supplies no --locked/--offline/profile flag. Cleanup removes the copied source and newly created examples directory in finally, but copying occurs before that guard; cleanup errors can mask the build error. It does not restore arbitrary build modifications or check final source cleanliness. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.py:23-62; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.py:86-108)

For each filename, compare both generated byte arrays, then either compare the checked fixture or immediately replace it with --write. A later mismatch can leave earlier fixtures replaced; publication is not atomic across the set. The printed hash is computed from first-run bytes and never compared against the README table. The Rust generator intentionally uses historical APIs, including previous::writer and version fields removed from current option structures; it should not be adapted to the code under test merely to make it compile there. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.py:109-129; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:12-35; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:102-228)

## Change boundaries

Changes to standard V2_0 finish and embedded serialization must preserve their different footer identities and must account for their separate buffer/metadata paths. Preparation ordering matters for validation before maybe_encode; row and page failure paths are not transactional. Extend the existing compatibility suite with independently generated stable baseline cases when compatibility is the concern; unstable V2_3 prior revisions carry no fixture obligation here. Full encoder/backend/Dataset callers and remaining V2 binary fixtures must still be analyzed before this is a complete implementation recipe. # V2_0 writer and exact-version compatibility harness

**PARTIAL CRATE COVERAGE.** This supplement covers 1,997 lines across the concrete V2_0 writer, testing helpers, compatibility tests and three fixture-provenance/generator files. The [shared reader](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md) covers current reader IO/cache orchestration. All six binary fixture payloads and complete legacy writer/reader internals are covered; delegated scheduling and complete encoding byte algorithms remain pending. Tests and generators were read, not run.

[Crate](rust-lance-file.md) · [Structural writers](rust-lance-file-structural-writer.md) · [Reader grammar](rust-lance-file-readers.md) · [Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [Contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) · [Build and tests](../L4-crosscutting/build-and-test.md)

## Concrete V2_0 ownership and initialization

Writer owns its own object writer, optional schema/type cache, field encoders, physical column metadata/mapping, per-field and aggregate row counts, global descriptors, schema metadata, boxed ArrayFieldEncodingStrategy, options and spill state. It does not compose the shared structural pipeline. Public Writer is reexported from its exact-version parent; the footer helper is effectively internal and reached through parent embedded-batch functions. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:153-218; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/mod.rs:21-32; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:852-856)

```text
V2_0 Writer
|-- ArrayFieldEncodingStrategy -> BatchEncoder -> FieldEncoder list
|-- schema + expected types + schema metadata
|-- physical column metadata + field mapping
|-- per-field counts -> aggregate maximum/logical length
|-- ObjectWriter + user global-buffer descriptors
'-- optional spill: Pending(store,path) -> Active(sidecar,chunk index)
```

Eager construction creates lazy state then initializes. Lazy construction stores inputs and allocates the default strategy without validation or IO. Initialization validates explicit options, computes cache/page limits, validates schema and constructs BatchEncoder before installing encoders/metadata/mapping. It divides a supplied total cache budget by top-level field count; with an empty schema this can divide by zero before schema validation. Defaults are 8 MiB per root field, 32 MiB max page, keep_original_array=false and alignment64. An explicit max-page value wins over the environment; malformed environment text warns and defaults, missing/non-Unicode text silently defaults, and an environment value of zero bypasses the explicit Some(0) rejection. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:184-218; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:326-369; rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:56-65)

## Preparation and row mutation

write_batch initializes from its first Arrow schema, checks ExpectedTypes, selects every required field by name and prepares every field array before testing for an empty batch or the single-batch u32 limit. Missing fields fail even for empty batches. FieldEncoder::prepare_array defaults to identity and documents preparation before state mutation; concrete validation/transformation remains encoder-defined. No separate recursive nullability walk appears in this writer. The structural pipeline instead performs its own logical-nullability validation. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:313-324; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:371-400; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:451-476; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:175-183; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:598-627)

Encoding snapshots each field's old row number, calls maybe_encode, writes out-of-line buffers, then checks aggregate u64 overflow. Counters advance before ordered page tasks and flush finish, so later failure does not rewind them. Batch counters use original batch.num_rows while encoding uses prepared array lengths; the caller/encoder relationship must preserve these lengths. write_column checks schema/index/input size/type, prepares one array, returns if that prepared array is empty, then advances only that field by its prepared length with unchecked addition and updates the aggregate maximum. A previously initialized lazy writer satisfies its schema check despite the explicit-schema wording in the error. Unequal root-field lengths are allowed. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:402-506; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:507-584)

FuturesOrdered emits task results in insertion order; pages are written sequentially, followed by writer flush. The first error stops the loop and drops remaining local futures. The code comment describes flush as observing failed uploads without waiting for all in-flight uploads; backend implementation, spawned-work cancellation and durability are still outside this scope. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:279-300)

## Buffer placement, spill and completion

Ordinary page, batch-external, global and column buffers get trailing 0x48 padding based on their payload length to64. Their starts are not repaired. V2_0 write_external_buffer writes completely raw at current position, unlike the structural sink's leading-zero alignment. Page metadata records raw lengths and wraps either page-description family in Any/Direct without checking the exact V2_0 grammar. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:41-41; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:231-262; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:703-708; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:831-849; rust/lance-file/src/writer/structural.rs:352-360)

Spill threshold per column is max(256 KiB/max(column_count,1),64). One message can overshoot; buffers retain capacity and chunk descriptors grow. Pending is removed before awaited sidecar creation, after page payload IO. A failed creation loses pending state. Finish removes metadata/spill state, shuts down and reopens the sidecar, reconstructs all pages for each column and replaces that column's prior page vector. Late spill can therefore discard descriptions retained before activation. Cleanup is explicitly caller-owned and no local deletion occurs. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:48-146; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:219-228; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:263-275; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:597-630)

finish flushes encoders, consumes/finishes them if present, writes descriptor and user-global table entries, column metadata, column offset table, global offset table, footer, then awaits shutdown. Descriptor and column metadata are raw protobuf bytes; each offset-table entry is a 16-byte LE(position,length) pair. Schema metadata is drained and blobs unloaded before descriptor IO. External-metadata initialization bypasses validation and replaces schema/metadata/aggregate rows without rebuilding encoder, type-cache, mapping or field-count state. It can support footer-only external output, but subsequent ordinary writes require coherent state the initializer does not establish. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:586-709; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:768-829)

Two position assumptions need preservation: finish_writers writes out-of-line buffers raw while the planner advances virtual positions by payload plus padding; column-buffer offsets advance by payload length while actual writes include padding. Multiple unaligned buffers can violate those assumptions. These are source deductions, not evidence that current encoder producers emit such shapes. The final physical-column count mismatch panics unconditionally. No finished flag or rollback protects repeat calls; abort is an empty async body and does not drop the writer. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:711-759; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:831-834; rust/lance-encoding/src/encoder.rs:130-159)

## Exact footer identity

| Footer-relative bytes | Standard V2_0 | Embedded V2_0 |
|---|---|---|
| 0–7 | column metadata start, LEu64 | same meaning |
| 8–15 | column offset table start, LEu64 | same meaning |
| 16–23 | global offset table start, LEu64 | same meaning |
| 24–27 | global-buffer count, LEu32 | zero in mini; one in self-described |
| 28–31 | physical-column count, LEu32 | page_table length |
| 32–33 | major0, LEu16 | major2, LEu16 |
| 34–35 | minor3, LEu16 | minor0, LEu16 |
| 36–39 | LANC | LANC |

These literal branches are independent implementations. The version decoder accepts both as V2_0, and tests distinguish standard and embedded mappings. concat_lance_footer copies input bytes and given page/column descriptors, optionally appends a cloned core schema without blob unloading, then metadata/tables/footer. It ignores ColumnInfo.index and top_level_columns and does not validate supplied buffer positions or grammar. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:812-828; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_0/writer.rs:852-952; rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:226-262; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:379-448)

## Compatibility fixture and test oracles

The deterministic input has 4,097 rows and five fields: Int32 IDs, nullable UTF8 names (every7th null), nullable Int32 lists (every11th null, every5th second child null), nullable Int8/UTF8 dictionary keys (every13th null), and nonnull LargeBinary payloads in a nullable blob-marked field. Compression metadata disables name and dictionary-value compression. Standard writers receive five batches of up to1,024 rows; embedded V2_0 uses only id/name for the first257 rows. (rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:36-98; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:232-315; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:401-408)

Stable cases compare complete current bytes to baseline includes, assert exact footer identity and read the baseline through the current reader. Read assertions include at least one multi-page physical column, full row count/schema equality and ordered value/null equality. Blob comparison ignores physical bytes under nulls. V2_3 instead writes twice in the same revision and checks equal bytes plus roundtrip; it has no checked historical fixture. The V1 test explicitly expects null lists as empty, null child integers as zero and null dictionary keys as green. The full V1 reader and writer are now independently traced in their supplements; this test still establishes only the stated fixture oracle. (rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:100-230; rust/lance-file/src/compatibility_tests.rs:318-524)

FsFixture exposes a local store, temp path and testing scheduler. write_lance_file collects the entire input, adds foo=bar to writer schema, finishes and returns original schema/data/mapping. read_lance_file requires that metadata, reads RangeFull with batch1024/readahead16 and collects all output. count_lance_file fully decodes/collects then sums rows. All use unwrap/assert rather than a fallible public result. The original returned schema does not receive the writer's added metadata. test_cache creates a fresh128MiB cache. (rust/lance-file/src/testing.rs:22-123)

## Provenance and generator failure boundaries

README pins baseline commit `3a72f8a61e14613f517dded6816d4bfc77817c93`, lists six SHA-256 values and requires using baseline writers for independent evidence. Local Git metadata confirms that commit exists; the six hashes match the inventory snapshot. No regeneration has been performed. The [V1 fixture](rust-lance-file-binary-fixtures.md) is now fully interpreted; both [embedded V2_0 fixtures](rust-lance-file-embedded-fixtures.md) are also fully interpreted, and the standard V2_2 binary payload is now fully interpreted. The pin identifies a commit and is not, by itself, proof of a released-package fixture. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/README.md:3-41)

The Python script checks exact HEAD and initial clean status, copies the Rust example into the baseline, then runs two separate Cargo processes with separate outputs and one shared isolated target directory. It supplies no --locked/--offline/profile flag. Cleanup removes the copied source and newly created examples directory in finally, but copying occurs before that guard; cleanup errors can mask the build error. It does not restore arbitrary build modifications or check final source cleanliness. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.py:23-62; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.py:86-108)

For each filename, compare both generated byte arrays, then either compare the checked fixture or immediately replace it with --write. A later mismatch can leave earlier fixtures replaced; publication is not atomic across the set. The printed hash is computed from first-run bytes and never compared against the README table. The Rust generator intentionally uses historical APIs, including previous::writer and version fields removed from current option structures; it should not be adapted to the code under test merely to make it compile there. (rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.py:109-129; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:12-35; rust/lance-file/test_data/exact_versions/datagen.rs:102-228)

## Change boundaries

Changes to standard V2_0 finish and embedded serialization must preserve their different footer identities and must account for their separate buffer/metadata paths. Preparation ordering matters for validation before maybe_encode; row and page failure paths are not transactional. Extend the existing compatibility suite with independently generated stable baseline cases when compatibility is the concern; unstable V2_3 prior revisions carry no fixture obligation here. Full encoder/backend/Dataset callers and remaining V2 binary fixtures must still be analyzed before this is a complete implementation recipe. # lance-file: file versions and entry points

**INCOMPLETE.** Fifty-five of 56 inventory entries are analyzed (25,581 physical text/symlink lines plus 1,640,495 binary bytes). ## Responsibility and routes

The crate declares readers/writers for the Lance file format. Its facade exports concat,datatypes,format,reader,testing,version,versions,writer; io is crate-visible with LanceEncodingsIo publicly reexported; compatibility_tests is private under cfg(test). Shared reader loading/cache/projection orchestration is covered in the [shared reader supplement](rust-lance-file-shared-reader.md); V1 foundations and concrete binary/plain/dictionary codecs are covered separately; the [full V1 reader](rust-lance-file-v1-reader.md) is covered. ## Caller requests and persisted identities

LanceFileVersion is a caller selector with Legacy,V2_0,V2_1,Stable,V2_2,Next,V2_3. Default is exact V2_2. resolve() maps Stable->V2_2,Next->V2_3 and exact variants to themselves (Legacy->V1). is_unstable is true only after resolving to V2_3. Display/serde preserve stable/next as strings; they are request serialization, not strict persisted identity codecs. (rust/lance-file/src/version.rs:19-127)

FromStr lowercases but does not trim. Accepted aliases are0.1/legacy,2.0/0.3,2.1,2.2,2.3,stable,next. ConcreteFileVersion has only V1,V2_0,V2_1,V2_2,V2_3, derives Hash but no ordering, and has no Default/serde/FromStr implementation here. ## Footer detection and errors

determine_file_version takes ObjectStore,Path,optional known usize size. If unknown, await store.size and checked-convert; if known, trust it. Reject size<8, await open_with_size and get_range(size-8..size), require footer[4..]==LANC, decode first four bytes as LEu16 major/minor and dispatch exact parser. IO errors propagate; size/magic/version errors are InvalidInput. Fewer than4 returned bytes could panic because no explicit received-length check precedes slicing. (rust/lance-file/src/lib.rs:25-60; rust/lance-file/src/format.rs:30-33)

This reads only the final8 bytes and does not verify pages, schema, full footer structure or data validity. The local async fixture uses synthetic8-byte legacy footers with no data. ## Extension boundary

Keep caller selectors distinct from exact storage identities; a new exact version needs explicit string/data-metadata/standard-footer/embedded-footer mapping and explicit capabilities elsewhere. Public FileConcatOptions exposes read_batch_bytes:usize and writer_options:FileWriterOptions. Default threshold is16*1024*1024 bytes plus writer defaults. Despite the maximum wording, batching never splits one page, so a single oversized page can exceed the threshold. Zero is rejected only in concat_prepared, after entrypoint metadata reads.

Public Copy/Clone/Debug/Eq FileConcatOutput contains exact version,u64 total physical rows,u64 object size. Written uses writer summary; Reused uses loaded input metadata file_size_bytes. No path, Dataset fragment ID or Blob ID lease is returned.

Public FileConcatReason starts with LegacyVersion, VersionMismatch(input_index,actual,expected), SchemaMismatch(input_index), ColumnLayoutMismatch(input_index,optional physical column) and ColumnEncodingMismatch(input_index,column_index). These are structured compatibility outcomes, not necessarily errors; indices are zero-based.

Remaining compatibility variants are ColumnBuffers(input/column/count), ExtraGlobalBuffers(input/count including schema) and BlobColumns. Column/global buffers lack relocation support at this layer. BlobColumns applies to the ordinary concat target schema; the validated-part path explicitly permits Blob schemas.

Display formats legacy/version/schema/layout/encoding reasons. Layout None denotes different physical-column count, Some identifies a physical column. Version display uses ConcreteFileVersion Display; messages do not include source paths here.

Display reports exact unsupported column/global buffer counts and a general Blob rejection string. It implements fmt::Display only; FileConcatReason is not declared an Error. These strings are used by higher-level callers to choose error/fallback presentation.

Public Eq FileConcatResult distinguishes Written(output), Reused(input index,output) and Unsupported(reason); Unsupported promises no output factory call. Private PreparedInput borrows input,metadata,schema for one attempt. encoded_column_encoding serializes ColumnInfo.encoding through protobuf Any into owned bytes; comparison is serialized column encoding equality, not page encoding equality.

check_compatibility first rejects any Blob in the ordinary target schema, then requires a first prepared input. It derives the baseline physical columns from the first input, descriptor-projects the target only for part mode, and serializes all baseline column encodings before checking input row/version/schema. It does not itself reject target V1; public ordinary dispatch handles legacy earlier.

Per-input check order is expected footer rows(InvalidInput), exact version(Unsupported VersionMismatch), complete Schema equality(Unsupported SchemaMismatch), exact external-metadata validation(CorruptFile wrapping any delegated error), then normalized/footer row equality(CorruptFile). No coercion, alias equivalence, column reordering or semantic encoding comparison is attempted.

After metadata validation, more than one global buffer gives Unsupported ExtraGlobalBuffers; schema buffer0 is regenerated. Different column count versus the first input gives ColumnLayoutMismatch(None), although prior schema/metadata checks may reject first. A zero-global buffer case has no local rejection here; valid readers normally require schema storage upstream.

Each physical column must have no column-level buffers, the same index as baseline and identical serialized column-level encoding. Error order is ColumnBuffers then index layout then encoding mismatch. Different page encodings/page counts are allowed if preceding validation succeeds. Returns None after every input; it never reads page payloads or validates their absolute ranges against EOF.

copy_page_buffers allocates output PageInfo capacity equal to page count and groups consecutive complete pages. For each page, checked offset+size rejects u64 range overflow and checked sum(size) rejects page byte-count overflow as contextual CorruptFile with path,input,column,page. There is no local offset+size<=file_size check; subsequent scheduler IO determines out-of-file behavior.

A page after the first in a batch is deferred when checked cumulative bytes overflow or exceed read_batch_bytes. The first page is always admitted, even oversized. The aggregate addition is then checked. Buffer counts include zero lengths but read ranges omit them; positive offset+size arithmetic is safe only because the earlier checked pass succeeded. Page boundaries/order are preserved, with no sorting/coalescing here.

One scheduler request at priority0 returns all positive-length ranges in the batch, or no IO occurs if none. Consume one returned Bytes per nonempty buffer; missing response or unequal byte length is contextual IO error, including overlong results under the short-read wording. Zero buffers consume no result but still call writer.write_external_buffer(empty). Each buffer is written sequentially and its new offset/size retained.

After writing all buffers of each page, clone its encoding, preserve num_rows and checked-add whole-input row_offset to priority. Priority overflow is InvalidInput after possible output writes. Extra returned buffers are rejected only after the batch writes. Retain relocated PageInfo for all pages; no page decoding, retry, checksum or rollback occurs in this helper.

concat_prepared is generic over a FnOnce async output factory. Reject zero read threshold, run compatibility, checked-sum footer row counts, and return Reused(0,metadata size) for exactly one ordinary input. This path never calls the factory or validates/uses writer_options. Part mode passes reuse_single_input=false and always creates output after checks, even for one part.

After all compatibility and total-row checks, await output factory and exact create_lazy_writer. Both calls are outside the write_result async block, so an error here does not invoke the explicit writer.abort branch below. Allocate one Vec<PageInfo> per first-input physical column and row_offset0. No metadata/page count memory budget or streaming footer builder exists here.

Traverse inputs in caller order and columns in metadata order, invoking exact copy_external_metadata_column with whether that output column already has pages. Its closure copies buffers and appends relocated pages. Checked row_offset advances once per input after all its columns. V2_0 dispatch may skip later structural header columns; V2_1/2/3 invoke every copy. This loop is sequential across files/columns and retains all output page metadata.

Finalize each output column through exact-version hook, then create ColumnInfo with baseline index/encoding, moved accumulated pages and an empty column-buffer vector. V2_0 structural header finalization reduces to one page with total rows/priority0; other current versions leave pages unchanged. Output page encodings can remain heterogeneous.

An empty external-buffer write aligns the upcoming schema descriptor. initialize_with_external_columns receives target schema clone, constructed columns and total rows; finish writes normal metadata/footer and shuts down. Success returns Written with exact target version and writer summary counts/size. Any error inside write_result awaits writer.abort then returns the original error; abort returns no Result here. There is no cancellation Drop guard, and cancellation before reaching the match does not execute this explicit abort.

Public concat_files documentation promises one metadata-read pass per input, pre-factory compatibility, no Arrow page decoding and regenerated offsets/priorities/structural metadata/footer. Doctest supplies a store.create async factory. Exact generic signature accepts borrowed target and ordered input slice, an owned FnOnce()->Future<Result<Box<dyn ObjectWriter>>> and owned options; no Send bound is imposed on that factory in this entrypoint.

concat_files rejects empty input before IO. try_join_all concurrently reads raw metadata for every input, retaining ordered results and propagating any read error. Only afterward, target V1 or any raw Legacy result returns Unsupported LegacyVersion, before expected-row/read-batch/ordinary Blob checks. Even a V1 target causes source metadata reads; invalid source may therefore return Err instead of Unsupported.

Finalize all current raw metadata through exact-version finish_metadata before borrowing it into PreparedInput; encountering Legacy here is an Internal defensive error after the earlier guard. Prepared schema is the actual file_schema, with no Blob normalization on ordinary path. Invoke concat_prepared with Blob disabled and single-input reuse enabled. Payload copying happens later and assumes caller-preserved immutable inputs.

Public concat_data_file_parts accepts validated DataFilePart slice with the same generic factory contract. It rejects empty parts, then compares every part optional BlobTargetId to the target optional ID, even if the schema is not Blob-bearing. None versus Some or different strings is InvalidInput before lease/compatibility/options checks. It does not validate Dataset/base authority from the opaque ID.

Clone every supplied lease together with original part index, sort by range start, and reject adjacent overlap when right.start<left.end, reporting both original indices/ranges. Touching endpoints are legal. This compares whole declared leases, even if no managed values used them or inputs are non-Blob; no per-value ID set is computed. None leases do not participate.

Build PreparedInput borrowing cached part metadata and normalized part schema, then concat_prepared allows Blob columns and disables reuse. No input metadata refresh or Blob revalidation occurs at assembly. DataFilePart::open is the capability boundary, while input immutability and target storage identity remain caller obligations.

Private cfg(test) module imports local ObjectStore,scheduler,CachedFileSize,temp paths,Atomics and AsyncWriteExt. write_file makes one Int32 value root from supplied i32 values, constructs a current exact writer with default options, writes once,finishes and returns schema. All fallible operations unwrap; helper is not a historical fixture generator.

input helper creates a testing ScanScheduler, opens the path with unknown size and attaches caller expected rows. The helper itself never compares the row count; only concat/open validation uses that option.

V2_1 concat success writes input values[1,2,3] and[4,5]. Atomic factory must run once; result must be Written with5rows; reopened metadata must report5rows,two pages and strictly increasing page priority. No payload RecordBatch is read, no exact offsets/sizes or byte equality are asserted despite the test name mentioning relocated metadata.

Same test concatenates the first input alone, supplies an error-returning counted factory, and requires Reused(0,_) plus zero calls. It does not assert reused output version/rows/size or compare input bytes.

Schema-metadata rstest runs V2_0,V2_1,V2_2,V2_3. Each fixture writes two identical[1,2] batches in separate files with schema key review-key=review-value. Defaults select all other writer policies; no nested type or Blob fixture.

Concat both metadata-tagged inputs and require Written. Reopen output metadata and assert schema key preserved. Expected4rows is merely stored in helper input then bypassed by direct read_all_metadata; no row-count assertion or decoded-value equality exists here.

Mixed-version test suppliesV2_1 thenV2_2 againstV2_1 target. Require Unsupported VersionMismatch at input1 and factory count0. Wildcard does not assert exact actual/expected fields and does not test target/schema/column incompatibility combinations.

Legacy test obtains target schema from a newly writtenV2_1 file, copies checked-in exact_versions/v1.lance bytes to a local object and shuts it down. It supplies expected rows0 for the legacy input, yet requires Unsupported LegacyVersion and factory0, illustrating legacy precedence before expected-row comparison. All six binary fixture contents are now fully interpreted in dedicated supplements.

White-box compatibility test loads a2rowV2_1 input and replaces its first ColumnInfo with one column-level buffer(0,1). Direct check_compatibility must return ColumnBuffers(input0,column0,count1). No serialized malformed file or output factory is involved.

Same white-box test clears normalized column_infos while preserving schema/footer, calls compatibility and asserts CorruptFile plus schema requires1physical columns substring. This tests external metadata validation before baseline column-count reasoning.

Same test clones normalized pages, decrements first num_rows by1 and rebuilds ColumnInfo. check_compatibility must return CorruptFile containing descriptor reports2physical rows. It mutates only in-memory normalized metadata, not file protobuf bytes, and does not exercise copy_page_buffers.

Overlap test uses ordinary Int32 non-BlobV2_1 files opened as DataFilePart with declared leases1..10 and5..20 and targetIDNone. Open accepts unused leases; both valid row expectations are1. No managed Blob descriptors or payloads are created.

Part concat overlap must produce an error naming both part0range1..10 and part1range5..20, and factory count remains0. Error variant is not asserted. This proves whole-declared-range overlap rejection even without Blob columns; not Blob-ID content validation.

Missing-input test writes valid and soon-deleted2rowV2_1 files, opens scheduler before deleting the latter, then concatenates both. Requires only is_err and factory0; no error type/message or missing-source recovery assertion.

Corrupt-input test writes literal not a Lance file, shuts down and concatenates with a valid input. It asserts only is_err. Its factory itself returns Err and has no call counter, so this oracle alone does not prove the factory was never called. File ends with seven tests(one four-version matrix) and two helpers. No local decoded-payload equality, Blob descriptor/null/container, zero-threshold, single-part-write, short/extra IO, abort/cancellation or overflow tests.

files.role: Public wrappers and trait conversions between flat protobuf fields/dictionary metadata and Lance core field trees; arena reconstruction preserves historical duplicate-ID tie-breaking. No file IO is performed.
ranges: SPDX and imports connect Arrow extension-name metadata, core Dictionary/Encoding/Field/LogicalType/Schema, Error/Result, HashMap and generated file protobuf. These conversions are shared schema boundaries, not an encoding implementation.

From<&pb::Field> is infallible despite the clippy allowance. Clone metadata keys and decode byte values with UTF-8 replacement, losing invalid original bytes. A nonempty dedicated extension_name overwrites the same metadata key; an empty dedicated name leaves an existing metadata extension intact.

Copy name/id/parent_id/nullability, wrap the logical type string, map numeric encodings 1 Plain,2 VarBinary,3 Dictionary,4 RLE and every other value to None. Start with no children and convert optional dictionary location; pb r#type is ignored. No logical-type, ID, encoding or dictionary-bound validation is performed here.

Primary-key position is Some(positive position), else Some(0) if the legacy primary-key boolean is true, else None. Clustering position is Some only for a positive position; its legacy boolean is ignored. These branches preserve primary-key legacy presence while clustering position zero decodes absent. Closing braces finish the field decoder.

From<&Field> for pb::Field copies IDs/name/logical-type/nullability, encodes string metadata as UTF-8 bytes and dictionary location, and maps the four Encoding variants to1..4, None to0. It does not recursively emit children; Fields handles flattening separately.

The protobuf field separately stores extension_name from core metadata or empty, forces r#type=0, sets legacy primary-key bool from Option presence and stores its position or0. It always writes legacy clustering bool=false and position or0. Core Some(0) primary survives via bool; Some(0) clustering would lose presence. No mutation of input.
Public tuple Fields owns Vec<pb::Field>. Private FieldNode owns one childless core Field plus child arena indices. No derives or validation occur in these declarations.

first_field_index_by_id iteratively traverses roots and children in pre-order using a LIFO stack populated in reverse order. Return first matching field ID, else None. Each call reserves up to all arena nodes and may scan all; it trusts internal indices. This reproduces the historical tree tie-break when duplicate IDs make a map lookup ambiguous.

From<&Field> for Fields recursively emits the parent followed by each child subtree in order, extending from newly built child Vecs. IDs/parent_id are retained, not reassigned or repaired. Deep trees still use recursive encoding and repeatedly move descendants through intermediate vectors; iterative decoding does not make all schema operations stack-safe.

TryFrom<&Fields> for Schema documents a flat pre-order list with parents before children, historical duplicates and legacy first-preorder matching. The compiling-style example reconstructs a single int32 root id0,parent-1 named value and asserts its name. Error associated type is core Error. The implementation actually requires earlier parents, not strictly contiguous pre-order input.

Preallocate nodes, root indices and HashMap<i32,Option<usize>> to input length. For each protobuf field, parent_id=-1 marks a root. Unique prior parent ID uses the constant-time map entry; duplicate marker None invokes DFS. Missing parent returns Schema with child name/id/parent and earlier-parent requirement. An impossible ambiguous-map/no-arena match returns Internal. Parent lookup happens before inserting this field, so no forward/self-new parent is accepted; referencing an earlier node with the same ID is possible.

Attach new arena index to parent or root list, convert the protobuf field, and insert its ID into the map. The second and every subsequent occurrence change the map entry to None, permanently marking ambiguity. Duplicate IDs are retained instead of rejected. Parent/root and child order are insertion order; valid unique-ID construction is expected linear hash-map work plus payload copies, while repeated ambiguous parents may make reconstruction quadratic.

Allocate Option<Field> slots and materialize nodes in reverse insertion order. Reserve each child list, take already built children in recorded order and set the parent slot. Missing/already-taken child is Internal with node index. Earlier-parent construction guarantees child indices are greater for normal inputs. No recursive reconstruction, but Field destruction and other consumers may still recurse.

Take root slots in recorded order, returning Internal if unexpectedly absent; collect through Result and return Schema with an empty metadata map. Empty field input yields an empty schema. No Schema::validate, uniqueness/type/nullability/key validation or parent-ID normalization follows reconstruction. Conversion errors discard temporary arena state without external effects.

Public FieldsWithMeta owns Fields plus HashMap<String,Vec<u8>> schema metadata, both public. TryFrom owned wrapper has core Error. Example supplies no fields and owner=lance bytes, then asserts decoded schema metadata; it does not validate a nonempty schema.

Owned schema metadata keys are moved and byte values lossily converted to strings before fallible field reconstruction. On success use its fields plus converted metadata, replacing the empty metadata map. Invalid UTF-8 is replacement-decoded; a later missing-parent error drops the converted metadata.

From<&Schema> for Fields flattens each top-level field subtree in order. From<&Schema> for FieldsWithMeta uses that flattening and clones the entire string metadata map before consuming values into bytes. Neither assigns IDs nor validates the input; there is no fallible result.

Dictionary protobuf i64 offset/length are cast directly to usize; values is always None. Reverse casts usize back to i64 and never serializes loaded dictionary values. Negative values/overflow/truncation are not rejected at this boundary; architecture width affects the cast. These are locations/counts, not loaded dictionaries.
Owned Encoding converts exhaustively to the matching protobuf enum, including RLE -> Rle. Unlike raw field encoding decode there is no unknown variant branch.

cfg(test) imports Arrow/core schema types and wrappers. Private proto_field helper sets id,parent_id,name,logical_type and leaves all other protobuf fields at Default. No historical fixture is loaded by this helper.

test_schema_set_ids constructs a,b-struct(f1,f2,f3),c Arrow fields, imports to core, flattens and asserts protobuf IDs exactly0..6. ID assignment comes from core import, not this flattening conversion. Does not assert parent IDs or roundtrip.

test_schema_metadata creates one int32 field plus k1/v1,k2/v2, imports core, encodes FieldsWithMeta, decodes and asserts Schema equality. Core Schema::PartialEq compares only fields (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:874-878), so this test does not actually assert preservation of the top-level metadata map. Only valid UTF-8 values are exercised.

Wide reconstruction fixture builds4096 root structs, each with two int32 children and unique IDs (12288 fields total). It asserts root count, every root ID/name, two-child count and both child IDs/names in order. No timing, allocation or logical-type assertion; source intent does not prove a performance bound.

Deep reconstruction fixture builds1024 nodes in a single chain, struct except final int32. It asserts one root, each ID/name, exactly one child until the leaf and no leaf children. Iterative traversal tests construction depth; no measured stack bound or claim about recursive serialization/drop.
Missing-parent fixture supplies child id7,parent42 and asserts Error::Schema plus contextual message substring. It does not separately exercise a forward reference where that parent appears later.

Duplicate-ID fixture lists root_a1,root_b2,nested_duplicate2 under root_a,then child3 parent2. Decoding attaches child beneath the nested duplicate, which appears first in reconstructed pre-order even though root_b appeared earlier in the flat list. It asserts both root/child shapes, pinning the historical tie-break.

Clustering fixture gives region Utf8 metadata position1,date Int32 position2 and unmarked value Float64. Core import and unenforced_clustering_key must return two fields ordered region,date. Metadata keys are exactly lance-schema:unenforced-clustering-key:position.

Roundtrip through FieldsWithMeta preserves both clustering field names and Some(1)/Some(2); value remains not a clustering key. No local tests for invalid UTF-8, unknown encodings, extension-name precedence, dictionary negative casts or primary-key legacy-position combinations. Module ends; no tests were run.

Core Field conversion has already been analyzed. Shared current reader and exact current writers are analyzed, and the complete V1 reader is now covered. all six pinned binary fixtures are interpreted; local roundtrip tests were read only.

files.role: Crate module facade and asynchronous footer-only exact file-version recognition.
ranges: SPDX; public concat,datatypes,format,reader,testing,version,versions,writer modules; io is pub(crate), compatibility_tests private cfg(test). Public LanceEncodingsIo reexport exposes selected IO type despite module visibility. Schema conversion, IO adapter, exact dispatch, writer facade and type checker are now covered; V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 concrete writers and shared structural pipeline are covered separately. The V2_0 writer, testing helpers, exact-version compatibility tests and fixture generator sources are also covered. writer_tests.rs is also fully analyzed. Shared reader metadata/index loading, local cache and read dispatch plus all its tests are now covered. Encoded-file concat compatibility, Blob part validation, page relocation and output lifecycle are now covered. The pinned V1, all three standard V2 and both embedded V2_0 binary fixtures are now fully interpreted in their supplements; all six binary fixtures are covered; delegated IO/decoder scheduling remains pending. Frozen V1 projection/mapping, dictionary dispatch, metadata conversion/batch grouping and dense page-table helpers are now covered; their concrete binary/plain/dictionary codecs are now covered; full V1 reader is now analyzed; backend lifecycle remains pending.

Imports shared MAGIC, core errors, ObjectStore/Path and exact version. determine_file_version(store,path,known_size)->Result<ConcreteFileVersion> obtains size via await store.size only if unknown, checked-converts it to usize or InvalidInput with path. Supplied usize size is trusted without checking actual length; no explicit size lookup then. Underlying open behavior is delegated, so this does not prove all HEAD requests avoided.

Reject size<8 with InvalidInput source text and path, then await open_with_size and exactly requested range size-8..size. Compare footer[4..] to MAGIC; mismatch returns contextual InvalidInput. No explicit received-length check: fewer than4 returned bytes can panic on slice; other non8 lengths fail magic comparison. Store/range IO errors propagate. No full file parse or schema/page integrity check.

Decode first two little-endian u16 values from four bytes, then delegate ConcreteFileVersion::from_footer_numbers. Magic match implies exactly8 returned bytes for this equality check. Unknown version error lacks path because decoder formats just the pair. The helper recognizes accepted footer aliases only and cannot establish complete file validity.

files.role: Frozen V1 file reader: public constructors, metadata/page-table cache keys, batch/range/take/statistics/stream APIs and private recursive Arrow reconstruction. Stores caller schema and dictionary values; no automatic schema discovery, row-ID synthesis or current-format grammar negotiation. Includes12 active tests and four helpers.
